description: BluegullAQITests hosts inside the real BluegullAQI app binary (TEST_HOST), which test-swift builds with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO. That means BluegullAQIApp's actual init()/@State property initializers ran for real as the test host process on every make test-swift invocation: LocationPermissionRequester(requestOnInit: true) fired the real system Location dialog every time (each unsigned test build is an identity TCC has never seen, so authorizationStatus reads as notDetermined and the request goes through), AQIRefreshController() started a real fetch loop hitting CoreLocation and the network, and the single-instance flock guard would exit(0) immediately (failing the whole test run with 'Early unexpected exit') if a real signed instance happened to already be running -- confirmed as a real failure earlier this session, not hypothetical. Steve noticed the recurring Location prompt and correctly guessed it was test-swift, not his own normal app launches.
acceptance_criteria: make test-swift never shows a system Location dialog and never makes a real network request, verified via log show (zero CFNetwork resuming entries, no requestWhenInUseAuthorization activity) during a real test-swift run. A real app-build/app-launch still requests permission and starts the fetch loop normally.
close_reason: Implemented: added BluegullAQIApp.isRunningTests (checks ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["XCTestConfigurationFilePath"] != nil, the standard signal XCTest sets on whatever process it hosts). Guards all three real side effects in the App struct: refreshController is nil under tests (AQIRefreshController.init? already models this), locationPermission uses requestOnInit: !isRunningTests (already-supported no-op mode), and init()'s single-instance flock returns early. Verified via log show during a real make test-swift run: zero CFNetwork resuming entries and no requestWhenInUseAuthorization activity (previously this fired every run); a subsequent real app-build/app-launch still shows one real fetch, confirming production behavior is unaffected. make test-swift passes (12 BluegullAQITests, 169 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() returns configuration=nil for every placed widget, so per-widget pinned locations never get fetched
description: AQIRefreshController.activeWidgetLocations() relies on WidgetCenter.shared.getCurrentConfigurations() to read each placed widget instance's SelectLocationIntent (an AppIntentConfiguration-based intent) so the container app can fetch/cache that widget's independently pinned location (bluegull-aqi-igu/mtm.21). Confirmed via temporary file-based debug logging (App Group container -- same technique bluegull-aqi-igu's own investigation used, since NSLog/os_log isn't reliably visible through log show/stream in this dev environment) with 4 real placed widgets, each manually configured to a distinct pinned location via right-click > Edit Widget: WidgetCenter returned all 4 WidgetInfo entries with the correct kind/family, but configuration was nil on every single one. This is a known real-world limitation of getCurrentConfigurations with AppIntentConfiguration-style widgets -- the intent doesn't reliably deserialize across the XPC boundary. Net effect: activeWidgetLocations() always returns [nil, nil, nil, nil] regardless of what each widget is actually pinned to, so refreshWidgetLocations() only ever fetches 'current location' (GPS), never any specific pin -- every widget pinned to a named location shows 'Data Unavailable' forever. bluegull-aqi-nmn's cache-rounding fix was necessary but not sufficient; this is the actual blocker for the behavior Steve is seeing right now (4 placed widgets, 4 changed locations, all showing Data Unavailable).
acceptance_criteria: Widgets configured to a specific pinned location actually get that location fetched and cached, verified against real placed widgets (not just unit tests, since the bug is in the WidgetCenter API boundary itself, which fakes can't reproduce). Needs a design decision first: the widget extension's own TimelineProvider DOES receive the correct SelectLocationIntent.location directly (it's not going through the buggy getCurrentConfigurations() path) -- likely fix is having the widget write its configured location into the shared App Group cache itself (a 'locations any widget currently wants' record) for the container app to read and fetch against, rather than relying on WidgetCenter to hand back each instance's configuration.
close_reason: Implemented: added WidgetRequestedLocationsStore (BluegullAQIKit) -- the widget extension's own TimelineProvider now writes its configured location (or a current-location marker) into the shared App Group cache on every entry computation, since it receives the real SelectLocationIntent directly from WidgetKit, unlike the container app going through the broken WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() path. AQIRefreshController.activeWidgetLocations() now reads from that store instead. Also added WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines(ofKind:) after a successful widget-location fetch (bluegull-aqi-mtm.12: the only sanctioned way to nudge a placed widget to redraw before its own ~1-hour reload policy fires) -- without it the underlying fix would be invisible on screen for up to an hour. Added 9 unit tests for the new store (WidgetRequestedLocationsStoreTests). Verified end-to-end against real placed widgets: one full clean run (empty App Group cache) correctly populated all 4 distinct rounded cache keys matching Steve's 4 real pinned locations (Home/Marlton/Manahawkin/Merchantville). Subsequent re-verification attempts were inconsistent -- confirmed this is bluegull-aqi-mtm.12's own documented limitation (WidgetKit throttles/staggers when it re-invokes a placed widget's provider outside of an attached Xcode debugger, with no supported CLI to force it), not a defect in this fix. Steve should confirm on his real desktop; if any widget still shows stale data, removing and re-placing it (or waiting for its next scheduled reload) forces a fresh timeline request. make test-swift passes (12 BluegullAQITests, 178 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: Widget cache lookups don't round location, so every pinned-location widget shows Data Unavailable
description: AQIFetchCoordinator caches a fetch result under reading.location, which AirNowDirectClient/BluegullServiceClient already round internally (bluegull-aqi-10h.11) -- the coordinator's own comment says a subsequent lookup needs cache.get(for: someLocation.rounded) to match. Three read call sites never rounded: WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot(for:), AQIRefreshController.refreshWidgetLocations' cache-miss check, and AQIRefreshController.fetchIfNeeded(for:). Confirmed against a real Group Container dump: 4 placed widgets pinned to 4 distinct locations, only one location's rounded coords happened to have a cache entry, and even that widget still showed Data Unavailable because the read-side key never matched. Existing WidgetTimelineComputerTests didn't catch this because they call cache.put and currentSnapshot with the exact same unrounded Location value, never exercising the write-rounds/read-must-round contract.
acceptance_criteria: Round the location at all three read call sites before calling cache.get. Add a regression test that writes under a rounded key (like AQIFetchCoordinator actually does) and reads with an unrounded pin, matching real usage.
close_reason: Implemented: rounded the location before every cache.get() lookup at all 3 read call sites (WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot, AQIRefreshController.refreshWidgetLocations' cache-miss check, and fetchIfNeeded) to match AQIFetchCoordinator's write side, which always caches under the fetch client's own rounded location. Added a regression test (testCurrentSnapshotForAPinFindsTheEntryCachedUnderItsRoundedCoordinates) that writes under a rounded key and reads with an unrounded pin, matching real usage -- also fixed an existing test that was unrealistically writing under the raw location, which is a write path production code never takes. make test-swift passes (12 BluegullAQITests, 169 BluegullAQIKit tests).

title: Widget location cache miss should fetch immediately, not wait for scheduled refresh
description: A widget pointed at a newly-set or never-before-fetched location shows 'Data unavailable' with a 'Last updated' caption that keeps advancing (misleadingly, since that timestamp is global -- AppGroupCache.lastSuccessfulFetchDate() records any fetch succeeding anywhere, not specifically this widget's location) while the actual reading for that location never arrives, because nothing fetches it promptly. AQIRefreshController only re-checks placed widgets' configured locations (activeWidgetLocations()) as a side effect of the menu bar's own ~1-hour RefreshScheduler cadence or an explicit menu-bar-location-change/permission-grant trigger -- there's no signal tied to 'a widget was just placed or reconfigured'. See plan at .claude/plans/inherited-skipping-sunrise.md (Issue 3).
design: Two parts: (a) WidgetDetailView runs in the container app process and already has everything needed to fetch -- its own doc comment admits 'opening this view isn't itself a signal to fetch,' which is the bug. Pass AQIRefreshController down from BluegullAQIApp and trigger refreshNow() for that specific location on appear when reading is nil. (b) The widget face itself (extension process) can't fetch -- give the widget-location half of AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() its own short-interval loop (~15-30s), separate from the menu bar's hourly cadence, so a newly-placed/reconfigured widget's location gets discovered and fetched quickly. WidgetCenter.getCurrentConfigurations() is a cheap local query, not a network call, so a short interval is safe; actual AirNow fetches stay exactly as rate-limit-bounded as today since an already-cached, unexpired location is a no-op via the existing dedup logic. Considered a Darwin-notification wake-on-cache-miss alternative; rejected as more IPC surface for the same practical outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Placing a new widget or changing an existing widget's location to something never-before-fetched results in real data appearing within roughly the settle interval, both on the widget face and in its detail window, without waiting for the scheduled refresh.
close_reason: Implemented both halves: (a) WidgetDetailView now takes AQIRefreshController (passed from BluegullAQIApp) and fetches on .task(id: location) when its cached reading is nil, updating an @State var so the view actually reflects the result; (b) added AQIRefreshController.widgetSettleLoop(), a ~20s companion to the hourly runLoop() that calls the new refreshWidgetLocations(mode:alreadyHandled:) -- extracted from refreshNow()'s widget loop, now with a cache.get(for:)==nil guard so it only ever fetches genuine cache misses, keeping frequent polling cheap and not multiplying AirNow request volume. Also added AQIRefreshController.fetchIfNeeded(for:) for the on-demand WidgetDetailView case. make test-swift passes (159 BluegullAQIKit tests + BluegullAQITests).

title: Widget location isn't actually independent -- new/unconfigured widgets mirror the menu bar's selection
description: Changing the menu bar's location changes what every desktop widget shows, when each widget is supposed to have its own independently-settable location (SelectLocationIntent, bluegull-aqi-mtm.3 -- the per-widget Edit Widget picker itself already works and is unchanged by this issue). Root cause: WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot(for:) treats a widget's nil configured location (both never-configured and explicit 'Current Location' collapse to nil) by calling cache.mostRecentEntry() -- literally whatever location was cached most recently anywhere, which in practice is usually the menu bar's own last fetch. AppGroupCache.mostRecentEntry()'s own doc comment already flags this as a pre-mtm.3 stopgap that was never followed through on for the nil case. See plan at .claude/plans/inherited-skipping-sunrise.md (Issue 2) for the full four-part fix.
design: Four parts, all detailed in the plan file: (a) give 'current GPS location' its own stable AppGroupCache slot (putCurrentLocation/getCurrentLocation) instead of relying on mostRecentEntry(), written by AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() whenever it resolves live GPS; (b) mirror the menu bar's current selection into the App Group so LocationOptionQuery.defaultResult() can seed a newly-placed widget with a one-time snapshot of it instead of the hardcoded .currentLocation; (c) thread a locationName through BluegullAQIWidgetEntry and render it on every widget family size; (d) reword the widget's gallery/Edit-Widget description text away from 'Local air quality' (implies wherever-you-are) to something location-neutral -- leave configurationDisplayName ('Current Air Quality') alone, that wording is compliance-guarded (ComplianceTests) and about data freshness, not location.
acceptance_criteria: New widgets default to the menu bar's location at creation time, not a live link. Each widget's location, once independently set via Edit Widget, is unaffected by later menu bar changes. Every widget family size displays its own location name. Widget gallery description no longer implies 'wherever you are'. make test-swift and swift test pass; golden snapshots updated.
close_reason: Implemented all four parts: (a) AppGroupCache.putCurrentLocation/getCurrentLocation give live-GPS its own stable cache slot, written by AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() whenever it resolves GPS (menu bar or a widget), read by WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot(for: nil) before falling back to mostRecentEntry(); (b) SharedMenuBarLocationStore mirrors the menu bar's selection into the App Group, written every refreshNow(), read by LocationOptionQuery.defaultResult() so a newly-placed widget snapshots the menu bar's current selection instead of always defaulting to the synthetic Current Location -- App Intents only calls defaultResult() once at placement time, so this is a one-time copy, not a live link; (c) BluegullAQIWidgetEntry carries locationName (from configuration.location?.name), rendered as a caption on every family size (Small/Medium/Large) and in the empty state; (d) widget's gallery/Edit-Widget .description() reworded from 'Local air quality at a glance' to 'Air quality for a location you choose' since 'Local' implied wherever-you-are. make test-swift and swift test both pass (159 BluegullAQIKit tests incl. new snapshot coverage); golden snapshots re-recorded via make record-snapshots and visually reviewed. Per-widget location selection itself (right-click widget -> Edit Widget) was already working (mtm.3) and is unchanged. Still needs Steve's live manual verification per the plan (add multiple widgets, confirm independence, confirm the menu bar's own later changes don't touch already-placed widgets).

title: Duplicate menu bar icon after Edit Widgets gallery launches a second app instance
description: App-launch via 'make app-launch' shows one menu bar AQI icon; adding a desktop widget via macOS's Edit Widgets gallery causes a second AQI icon to appear in the menu bar, almost certainly a second BluegullAQI process. BluegullAQIApp.swift has no single-instance guard -- LSUIElement is true, no LSMultipleInstancesProhibited, and nothing checks NSRunningApplication for an existing instance before building the MenuBarExtra scene. See plan at .claude/plans/inherited-skipping-sunrise.md (Issue 1).
design: Add a single-instance guard in BluegullAQIApp.init(), the earliest hook before any Scene is built: check NSRunningApplication.runningApplications(withBundleIdentifier:) for another running process with a different pid; if found, activate() it and exit(0) immediately, before the menu bar item can ever appear. exit(0) rather than NSApp.terminate since AppKit's lifecycle isn't fully spun up yet inside App.init().

title: Widget-configured locations never get fetched unless menu bar also shows them
description: AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() only ever fetches ONE location: whatever MenuBarLocationSelectionStore currently resolves for the menu bar's own picker (e70.21). It does not loop over pinned locations or enumerate active widget configurations. But each desktop widget instance has its own independent location via SelectLocationIntent/WidgetLocationOptions (mtm.3), reading from the same App Group cache keyed by location coords. If a widget is configured to a location the menu bar isn't currently showing, its cache entry is never populated/refreshed -- the widget is stuck at 'No Data' or a stale reading indefinitely, since nothing else ever fetches for it. Confirmed against real Group Container data (group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.plist): 3 pinned locations exist (Home, Syracuse, Seattle), but only 2 have cache entries (Home, Syracuse) -- Seattle has never been fetched, and the two that do exist line up with manual menu-bar toggling, not independent per-widget refresh.
acceptance_criteria: Every location actually in use by a placed widget (or at minimum every pinned location) gets refreshed on the normal schedule, independent of what the menu bar happens to be showing. Needs a design decision first: fetch every pinned location each cycle (simplest, multiplies AirNow request volume by pinned-location count) vs. enumerate actual active widget configurations via WidgetKit's WidgetCenter API (fetches only what's really placed, more precise, more complex) -- affects q9r's rate-limit/cache-miss budget in Service mode, so Steve should pick the approach.
close_reason: Implemented: moved SelectLocationIntent/LocationOptionEntity/LocationOptionQuery from the widget extension target into BluegullAQIKit (new SelectLocationIntent.swift) so the container app can import and interpret them too -- added BluegullWidgetKind.aqi as a shared kind-string constant. AQIRefreshController.refreshNow() now calls WidgetCenter.shared.getCurrentConfigurations() (wrapped as an async extension) to enumerate every currently-placed widget instance, extracts each one's configured SelectLocationIntent.location, and fetches+caches every distinct location (deduped via Location.rounded against the menu bar's own already-fetched location) in addition to the menu bar's own single selection -- which is all it fetched before. Errors on these extra fetches don't touch lastError/latestReading, which still describe only the menu bar's own display. Verified end-to-end with temporary file-based debug logging (App Group container, since NSLog wasn't visible to log show/stream in this dev environment): WidgetCenter correctly returned all 3 real placed widget instances (small/medium/large) with correct kind/family. All 3 currently show nil configuration (never individually set to a pinned location yet -- that's a separate manual step for Steve to try via right-click > Edit Widget), which is why this fix alone didn't retroactively populate Seattle's cache entry; the mechanism itself is confirmed working. make test-swift (12 BluegullAQITests) and swift test (159 BluegullAQIKit tests) both pass.

title: Select and document the AirNow endpoint(s) to call
description:
The API Fact Sheet enumerates several web services with meaningful differences, and the design has been loosely referencing 'currentobservation/latLong' without confirming it's the right one:

  - Current Observations by Reporting Area -- 'Real-time air quality observations (NowCast AQI) for each pollutant measured by reporting areas -- cities or other reporting areas DEFINED BY AIR QUALITY AGENCIES.' Appears to match our needs on all three axes: NowCast, per-pollutant breakdown (widget scope), and reporting-area scoping.
  - Observations by Monitoring Site -- site-level rather than aggregated.
  - Forecasts / Historical Observations by Reporting Area / Contour Maps -- not v1.

Confirm which endpoint actually returns: (a) NowCast AQI, (b) the full per-pollutant breakdown the widget scope requires, (c) the owning agency name for attribution, and (d) a category descriptor, or whether we derive the category from the value against the TAD table (allowed -- that's classification of a received AQI, not computing an AQI; distinct from bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

The 'reporting areas defined by air quality agencies' phrasing is likely where attribution comes from -- airnow.gov showed 'San Francisco Reporting Area' and 'Data courtesy of Bay Area Air District' together. Feeds directly into bluegull-aqi-10h.15. Record the answer in doc/DESIGN.md.
close_reason:
RESOLVED with live-verified evidence, not just documentation reading. The 'classic' endpoint (/aq/observation/latLong/current/) most training data/tutorials reference is being retired by EPA on 2026-09-30 -- found via a dated, merged pyairnow PR migrating for exactly this reason, confirmed directly against EPA's own official PDF notice (AirNowAPIUpdates2026June.pdf), then confirmed live with an actual test query.

Correct endpoint: GET https://www.airnowapi.org/aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/ (?format=application/json&latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&API_KEY={key}). Response: JSON array, one object per pollutant: dateObserved, hourObserved (string 'HH:MM'), localTimeZone, reportingAreaName, siteID, siteName, parameterName, nowcastAQI, aqiCategoryName, reportingAgency, lookupBehavior, consideredMonitors, lookupBoundary. Error shape: {"WebServiceError":[{"Message":"..."}]}. Empty array = no data.

Answers all four original questions: (a) NowCast AQI -- yes, nowcastAQI field. (b) full per-pollutant breakdown -- yes, one array entry per pollutant. (c) owning agency name for attribution -- yes, reportingAgency field, confirmed present and populated ('Bay Area Air District') in a live response, directly answering bluegull-aqi-10h.15 with no fallback needed for the common case. (d) category descriptor -- yes, aqiCategoryName (no numeric Category.Number in the raw response, unlike the retiring endpoint -- derive the number from the TAD table if needed, that's classification of a received value, not computing an AQI, per bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

Recorded in doc/DESIGN.md 'Backend service' architecture section since both the backend (bluegull-aqi-q9r.2) and AirNowDirectClient need this same endpoint.

title: Never derive AQI client-side; display values as received
description:
HARD CONSTRAINT from two independent sources. The AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require data be 'disseminated as received' without alteration. The TAD independently states it is 'not valid to use shorter-term (e.g. hourly) data to calculate an AQI value.'

So: display AirNow's AQI values exactly as returned. NEVER convert a pollutant concentration into an AQI, never re-derive, never interpolate, never round differently than received. The TAD's breakpoint table (Table 5) and interpolation formula (Equation 1) are in the design doc as documentation of what NOT to implement -- they are the agency-side calculation, not ours.

If the API returns a raw concentration for some pollutant WITHOUT an accompanying AQI value, display the concentration labeled as a concentration (with units) -- do not compute an index from it.

Include a test asserting no AQI-derivation logic exists in the codebase (e.g. no breakpoint table, no interpolation against one), so this can't be reintroduced later by someone trying to 'fill in' a missing value. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.
close_reason: Added ComplianceTests.swift: scans every .swift file under Sources/ (comments stripped) for identifiers that would only appear in client-side AQI derivation (breakpoint, interpolat, computeAQI, deriveAQI, calculateAQI, etc). Verified the guard actually works by temporarily injecting a computeAQI function, confirming the test failed, then restoring the file -- not just that it passes on innocent code. The substantive constraint (never derive/re-derive an AQI) was already satisfied by construction from bluegull-aqi-10h.2: AQICategory.init(aqi:) only consumes AirNow's own nowcastAQI value, and PollutantReading has no concentration/breakpoint field to derive from in the first place. 16/16 tests pass via swift test.

title: Round coordinates client-side before transmission
description:
Privacy by design, and free. The service otherwise receives precise coordinates and logs requests, accumulating 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' in CloudWatch for the whole retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database, and a poor fit for an app whose purpose is local environmental data.

AirNow resolves to the nearest monitoring station regardless, so ~1km precision loses no accuracy AND improves cache hit rates. Round before the request leaves the Mac so the server never receives a precise location at all. Applies to both Direct and Service mode.
close_reason: Location.rounded rounds to ~1km precision (2 decimal degrees), deliberately matching the server's LOCATION_KEY_PRECISION in cache.py exactly for cache-hit-rate alignment, not just privacy. AirNowDirectClient rounds before building the request -- AirNow never receives a precise coordinate regardless of caller precision; returned AQIReading.location is the rounded value too. Added a note to bluegull-aqi-10h.4 (BluegullServiceClient, not yet built) so the same treatment isn't missed there. Updated two existing tests that asserted exact unrounded coordinates, added a new rounding-correctness test (not just truncation) at a .5 boundary. 61/61 tests pass via swift test.

title: Set up AWS Budget alarms before first deploy

title: Add cost circuit breakers: reserved concurrency + API Gateway throttling
description:
Denial of wallet is the primary threat on this architecture. Lambda, API Gateway, and on-demand DynamoDB all scale elastically, so they all BILL elastically -- a sustained flood costs money at a rate nothing in the base design bounds. Per-IP WAF rate limiting does little against a botnet, and WAF bills per request itself, amplifying cost under attack rather than capping it.

  - Lambda reserved concurrency: a hard ceiling on concurrent executions and therefore on cost per unit time. This is the PRIMARY circuit breaker, not just a noisy-neighbor courtesy -- note the existing scale-config task frames it that way and should be read together with this one.
  - API Gateway stage throttling: hard request-rate cap, independent of WAF.
  - DynamoDB on-demand has no ceiling by design; the Lambda cap is what indirectly bounds it.
close_reason: Added LambdaReservedConcurrentExecutions parameter (default 20, conservative for a project sharing this AWS account with Plant-Tracer) wired to AqiFunction.ReservedConcurrentExecutions -- the primary denial-of-wallet circuit breaker. Added ApiThrottlingRateLimit/ApiThrottlingBurstLimit (defaults 10/20) wired to AqiHttpApi.DefaultRouteSettings, independent of WAF (not deployed yet) and of the Lambda ceiling. All three are SAM Parameters, adjustable per environment via parameter_overrides without a code change. sam validate --lint and sam build both succeed; 35/35 tests still pass (no code changes, template-only).

title: Validate coordinates and reject out-of-coverage requests
description:
Closes the cache-cardinality attack, which the stampede mitigation does NOT cover: stale-while-revalidate + single-flight collapses concurrent requests for the SAME key, so an attacker requesting a million DISTINCT coordinates produces a million cache misses, each triggering an upstream AirNow call -- burning the AirNow quota (likely getting the key banned), filling DynamoDB with junk, and running up Lambda cost.

Required:
  - Validate lat/long are numeric, in range, and sanely bounded.
  - Reject coordinates outside AirNow's coverage area BEFORE any upstream call. A request for the middle of the Pacific should cost a 400, not an AirNow request.
  - Snap to a coarse grid so total cache key cardinality is finite and bounded.
close_reason: Implemented in coverage.py: validate_coverage() rejects physically invalid coordinates and anything outside a generous North America bounding box (CONUS/Alaska/Hawaii/Puerto Rico/Canada/Mexico) before aqi_lookup.get_aqi() even instantiates the cache client -- closes the cardinality-attack gap that stale-while-revalidate/single-flight (q9r.15) doesn't cover. Cache-key grid-snapping was already done via cache.location_key()'s 2-decimal rounding (q9r.2). Fixed two pre-existing tests that used non-North-American coordinates (London; a point south of the box). Verified live via make run-local against the real AirNow API: valid US location succeeded, Pacific/Europe/out-of-range-latitude all returned 400 with no AirNow call or cache-log line. 35/35 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Use GitHub Actions OIDC role assumption for AWS deploys
description: Assume an AWS role via OIDC rather than storing long-lived access keys in GitHub secrets -- no durable credential exists to leak, and access is scoped and auditable. Requires an IAM role with a trust policy for GitHub's OIDC provider, restricted to this repo.
close_reason: Created GitHub OIDC provider + bluegull-aqi-github-deploy IAM role (arn:aws:iam::843088391598:role/bluegull-aqi-github-deploy), scoped to bluegull-aqi-* resources (service/iam/). Surfaced and resolved a release/rollback design gap: dev+stage deploy from any branch, prod only from a vX.Y.Z tag, enforced both in-workflow (deploy.yml-OFF guard) and via a GitHub Environment tag policy on prod. AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN repo secret set. Documented in doc/DESIGN.md.

title: Redact AirNow keys and raw coordinates before logging
description:
TWO separate leaks, same discipline.

1. CREDENTIAL. AirNow passes its API key as a URL query parameter (...&API_KEY=...), so logging the request URL writes the key straight into CloudWatch Logs, readable by anyone with log access for the whole retention period. This is the likeliest way this project leaks a key and it looks exactly like ordinary debug logging.

2. PRIVACY. Logging raw coordinates accumulates 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' for the retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database. Clients round coordinates before sending (see the client-side rounding task), but the service must not log even rounded values at full fidelity or tie them to source IPs.

Also ensure error responses and stack traces never echo the upstream URL or request headers back to clients. Needs a test asserting neither the key nor raw coordinates appear in log output.

Also fixed a related gap: logging.basicConfig was setting root level from LOG_LEVEL, which unmuted botocore's own DEBUG logging (raw DynamoDB item bodies) -- root now pinned at WARNING, only the app logger tree honors LOG_LEVEL. 7 new tests in test_logging_redaction.py, verified live via make run-local under LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG. 21/21 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Add gitleaks pre-commit hook and CI scan
description:
Two layers: a pre-commit hook catches a secret locally before a commit exists (cheapest possible point), and a CI job backstops commits made without the hook installed -- fresh clones, other machines, other agents.

CRITICAL -- must include a CUSTOM RULE for the AirNow key. GitHub's push protection and gitleaks' default rules both key on distinctive credential formats (AWS 'AKIA...', GitHub 'ghp_...', Stripe 'sk_live_...'). The AirNow key has no such distinctive prefix -- like most government API keys it is a generic token -- so NO pattern scanner will reliably catch a bare one. Default protection therefore covers the AWS and Apple credentials in our inventory but NOT the project's primary secret.

The custom rule must key on context rather than the token shape: assignments to AIRNOW_API_KEY / API_KEY, and any high-entropy token appearing near 'airnowapi.org'. Without this, the layered enforcement described in doc/DESIGN.md has a hole exactly where it matters most.
close_reason: Implemented with Betterleaks (gitleaks' actively-developed drop-in-compatible successor -- gitleaks itself is now feature-complete/maintenance-only, confirmed via web research after Steve flagged its README warning). .betterleaks.toml extends the default ruleset with two custom rules keyed on context (AIRNOW_API_KEY/API_KEY assignment, and a token following API_KEY= on a line containing airnowapi.org) since the AirNow key has no distinctive prefix for shape-based detection. Verified rules against real/placeholder values via betterleaks stdin and against the full repo git history (zero false positives, zero pre-existing leaks). Local hook wired into .beads/hooks/pre-commit (not a separate pre-commit-framework config, which conflicts with Beads already owning core.hooksPath -- confirmed by trying it and reading the refusal). CI backstop added at .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml, pinned to v1.7.2 with checksum verification, dry-run tested locally. Verified live end-to-end: staged fake AIRNOW_API_KEY value was blocked by the hook; clean commit still succeeded.

title: Implement perf baseline storage and regression gate
description:
Two independent checks per metric: an ABSOLUTE ceiling and a RELATIVE regression gate. They catch different failures -- the relative gate catches a sudden jump but is blind to the ratchet (drift 4% eleven times and you've doubled without ever failing a build); the absolute ceiling stops that.

Absolute ceilings (server-side latency, measured API Gateway receive -> response send):
  - Warm cached round-trip: p95 < 50ms, p50 < 25ms
  - Uncached round-trip, AirNow stubbed: p95 < 100ms
  - Cold start Init Duration: p50 < 600ms, investigate > 1s
  - p95 latency at 100 concurrent: within 2x the 10-concurrent p95
  - Error rate at 10 and 100 concurrent: < 0.1%
  - Cache hit ratio under steady-state load: > 95%

Relative gates: 5% on everything except cold start (~15%, variance is inherently larger). Compare percentiles over N>=100 samples, never single measurements.

Baseline lives in perf-baseline.json committed to the repo, so regressions appear as a reviewable diff and accepting an intentional regression is an explicit commit rather than a silent overwrite. Real end-to-end uncached latency (live AirNow) is recorded for observability but NOT gated -- it mostly measures AirNow, which we don't control. Client-observed latency likewise tracked but not gated (DNS/TLS/distance dominate; no code change fixes them).

title: Add AirNow stub/test mode for load testing
description: MANDATORY before any load test runs, not an optimization: driving 100 concurrent uncached requests at the live AirNow API would burn the project's quota and plausibly violate its terms. Env-gated test mode (or a reserved synthetic location) on the dev stage returns canned data in place of the upstream call, so load tests measure our overhead without touching AirNow.
close_reason: New airnow_stub.py gates canned data on BOTH AIRNOW_STUB_MODE=1 AND the reserved synthetic coordinate (40.0, -100.0) -- either alone is not enough, so a real request can never accidentally get stubbed and the reserved coordinate behaves normally when the env var is unset. Deliberately not a template.yaml env var so it can't be baked into a deployed stack by accident; enabling it for an actual load test run is out-of-band, out of this task's scope. Wired into aqi_lookup.get_aqi() so stub responses still flow through the real cache path (only the AirNow HTTP call is replaced) and key resolution is skipped for stub requests. Verified live via make run-local: fresh miss served from stub with a distinct log line, then cache hit; same coordinate without the env var correctly falls through to a real AirNow call. 42/42 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Test concurrent cache-miss behavior against DynamoDB Local
description: Verify the stampede mitigation actually works: concurrent misses on the same key must produce exactly one upstream AirNow call, and an expired entry must be served immediately rather than blocking. Runs against DynamoDB Local -- no AWS needed.
close_reason: Added test_concurrent_cache.py: real threading.Thread-based races (not a simulated lock like the rest of test_aqi_lookup.py) verifying concurrent cache misses on the same key produce exactly one AirNow call, and that an expired entry is served immediately rather than blocking behind the request revalidating it. This is deliberately the kind of test that would have caught the two real concurrency bugs found and fixed in q9r.15 (a PutItem-clears-the-lock race and a TOCTOU gap between miss-check and lock-acquisition), both of which were only actually caught via live testing against a real ThreadingHTTPServer, not by simulated-lock unit tests.

title: Implement stale-while-revalidate + single-flight cache logic
description: The core horizontal-scaling mechanism. On a miss against an expired entry: serve the stale value immediately, and let exactly one request win a DynamoDB conditional-write lock to refresh it in the background. AirNow must see at most one call per location per TTL regardless of client concurrency. Cold-start-of-the-world (no entry at all) may block -- that's a once-per-location event. Cache TTL should align to AirNow's hourly publish schedule rather than being a rolling hour from first request.
close_reason: Implemented stale-while-revalidate + single-flight via Cache.get_stale(), Cache.try_acquire_refresh_lock() (DynamoDB conditional UpdateItem), and TTL alignment to the next boundary since epoch (cache.seconds_until_next_boundary()) rather than a rolling window. Two real concurrency bugs found and fixed via live testing under genuine thread/process concurrency (not just simulated-lock unit tests): (1) Cache.put() used PutItem which wiped the lock attribute early, letting a slower request acquire a fresh lock and redundantly re-fetch -- fixed by switching to UpdateItem touching only Data/FetchedAt/ExpiresAt. (2) A TOCTOU race between a request's own miss-check and its own lock-acquisition -- fixed by re-checking the cache immediately after winning the lock. Also fixed bin/run_local.py to use ThreadingHTTPServer instead of the single-connection HTTPServer, since the latter made it impossible to observe real concurrent-request behavior locally at all. Added the missing dynamodb:UpdateItem IAM permission to template.yaml. Verified live at 10 and 20 genuinely concurrent requests against real AirNow: exactly one AirNow call per batch each time. 57/57 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10, sam validate --lint clean.

title: Define shared models: AQIReading, PollutantReading, Location
description:
Common models both data-source clients decode into, so callers don't care which source answered.

MUST include the official EPA AQI category table as a single shared mapping -- not left for each UI target to define separately. Values below are verbatim from the AQI Technical Assistance Document (EPA 454/B-18-007, Sept 2018), Tables 1 and 2. These are binding by incorporation: the AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require values be 'disseminated in accordance with the AQI and corresponding RGB colors as directed in the Technical Assistance Document.'

  RANGE      DESCRIPTOR                      COLOR    RGB            HEX
  0-50       Good                            Green    0, 228, 0      #00E400
  51-100     Moderate                        Yellow   255, 255, 0    #FFFF00
  101-150    Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  Orange   255, 126, 0    #FF7E00
  151-200    Unhealthy                       Red      255, 0, 0      #FF0000
  201-300    Very Unhealthy                  Purple   143, 63, 151   #8F3F97
  301-500    Hazardous                       Maroon   126, 0, 35     #7E0023

GOTCHAS: Green is 0,228,0 -- NOT 0,255,0. Maroon is 126,0,35 -- not a generic dark red. Getting these subtly wrong is the most likely failure mode.

SPECIFY IN sRGB EXPLICITLY. On a wide-gamut Display P3 Mac, a color literal interpreted in the display's native color space renders visibly different values than EPA specified.

Full descriptor is 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups'; 'USG' is AirNow's own abbreviation for tight layouts (seen on airnow.gov's legend) and is acceptable where space genuinely requires it.

AQI values above 500 are 'Beyond the AQI' and need separate handling -- see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.
notes: AQI category scale is bounded at 500 per TAD Table 1 (301-500 Hazardous). Values above 500 are 'beyond the AQI scale' -- valid but off-scale data, not an error; see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. The model must represent that case rather than leaving it unmapped.

PollutantReading's property names match AirNow's JSON keys exactly (including siteID's capitalization) so Codable synthesis needs no manual CodingKeys; nowcastAQI is optional per bluegull-aqi-10h.17's raw-concentration-without-AQI case. AQICategory is the single shared TAD Table 1/2 mapping (verbatim colors/descriptors, verified with boundary + exact-color tests) and handles >500 as .beyondAQI per bluegull-aqi-10h.16. Colors are a plain AQIColor byte-triple, not Color/NSColor, keeping the package UI-framework-free -- callers apply sRGB explicitly at point of use. title: Helper needs a MachService so the app can start it on demand
description:
Enabling work for hib.6's first-run design, not currently covered by any other issue in this epic.

THE GAP: the app needs to start the helper AT A CHOSEN MOMENT -- specifically, right after the user agrees to turn on background updates, so the location prompt lands while they are still looking at the thing that asked. Nothing in the epic currently provides that.

Registration does not start it. hib.10 measured runs=0 and state="not running" immediately after a successful SMAppService.agent register(), which is correct behaviour for a job with no RunAtLoad and no KeepAlive -- and that on-demand shape is the whole point of the design, so it should not be changed. Waiting for the XPC activity to fire naturally is exactly the uncontrolled timing hib.6's first-run design rejects: in the hib.10 probe the first firing came ~70 seconds after registration, and with the production Interval it would be minutes to hours.

WHAT IS NEEDED: a MachServices entry in the helper's launchd plist, and an XPC connection opened from the app. Connecting is what demand-starts the job -- the same mechanism weatherd uses (its plist declares eight MachServices). This is the one piece of weatherd's shape the hib.10 spike deliberately skipped, because it was orthogonal to the wakeup question being tested.

SANDBOX CONSTRAINT, THE REAL RISK HERE AND WORTH TESTING BEFORE ANY OF hib.6 IS BUILT ON IT: a sandboxed app cannot look up an arbitrary global mach service name. The route that is acceptable for App Store distribution is a service name prefixed with the app group identifier (group.solutions.bluegull.aqi...). The alternative, com.apple.security.temporary-exception.mach-lookup.global-name, is a temporary-exception entitlement and a poor thing to carry into App Review (fw4.8 already notes the helper adds review surface; this would add more).

Both processes are sandboxed, which is the case least likely to "just work" and the one that matters -- an unsandboxed test would prove the wrong thing, the same trap that made the hib.10 agents sandboxed on purpose.

Cheap to test: spike/hib10/ already has a signed, sandboxed container app and a signed, sandboxed agent that talk to nothing. Adding a MachServices key and a connection attempt is a small change to a harness that already works, and it does not need a fresh bundle id -- no TCC grant is involved, so unlike hib.10's question 5 this experiment is repeatable.
acceptance_criteria: From the sandboxed container app, opening an XPC connection to an app-group-prefixed mach service demand-starts the sandboxed helper, verified by a PROCESS_START log line with ppid=1 appearing within a second of the connection attempt, on a job with no RunAtLoad. If the app-group prefix does not work, the finding and the reason are recorded so hib.6's first-run design can be reworked before it is built.
close_reason: Closed

comments.text:
ANSWERED: YES, via the app-group-prefixed name -- the route that is clean for App Store review. Measured 2026-09-01, both processes sandboxed, both Developer ID signed.

FULL ROUND TRIP, from a job with NO RunAtLoad, NO KeepAlive and NO LaunchEvents of any kind:

  before the ping:  state = not running, runs = 0
  ping group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.hib10: REPLY from pid 63305 via group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.hib10
  after the ping:   state = running, runs = 1

  agent log, same second:
    PROCESS_START pid=63165 ppid=1 mode=machsvc
    LISTENING name=group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.hib10
    MACH_CONNECTION_ACCEPTED name=group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.hib10

That plist declares no schedule at all, so nothing else could have started the process. The connection did. Latency start-to-accepted was ~3ms (16:07:06.179 start, .182 accepted), which is far better than hib.6's first-run flow needs -- the user will not perceive a gap between agreeing and seeing the system prompt.

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS AS USEFUL AS THE POSITIVE. G5DWPBWHQ5.hib10.svc -- the team-identifier prefix -- returned "Connection invalid", from the same app, in the same run, against the same agent which WAS listening on that name (LISTENING logged for both). So the app-group result is not an artifact of something being generally permissive: the sandbox is genuinely enforcing a rule, and an application-group entitlement value is what satisfies it. Both ends carry com.apple.security.application-groups with group.solutions.bluegull.aqi, the same group the shipping app and widget already share, so the production helper needs no new entitlement beyond what it wants anyway for the cache.

CONSEQUENCE: hib.6's first-run design is buildable as drafted. The app can register the agent and then start it at a chosen moment, so the location prompt arrives while the user is still looking at the thing that asked. No temporary-exception entitlement is needed, so fw4.8's review surface does not grow.

ONE TEST-CODE BUG WORTH RECORDING, because it produced a convincing false negative on the first run: the app's first attempt reported "no reply" for the app-group name even though the agent had logged MACH_CONNECTION_ACCEPTED and MACH_MESSAGE received. The mechanism was fine. xpc_connection_send_message_with_reply was handed DispatchQueue.main while the calling code -- running in the app's init(), before NSApplication starts -- blocked that same thread on a DispatchGroup.wait(). The reply could not be delivered until the wait timed out. Anyone wiring this into the real app should not do a synchronous wait on main; the production flow wants the reply asynchronously anyway, since the app is meanwhile showing a "waiting for permission" state.

STILL NOT COVERED HERE (deliberately, it belongs in hib.4/hib.6): what the app and helper actually SAY to each other. This proved the channel opens and demand-starts the job; it did not define a protocol. For the first-run flow the message can be as thin as "run your first-run sequence now".

title: Consider auto-registering launch-at-login on first launch (opt-out, not opt-in)
description:
PROPOSAL, not decided -- needs Steve's product call.

Today (v0.2.1, bluegull-aqi-fvt) launch-at-login is DEFAULT OFF. LaunchAtLoginToggle.swift calls SMAppService.mainApp.register() only from an explicit user toggle in Settings; nothing registers on first launch. So a user who never opens Settings gets no background presence at all, and every "Current Location" widget they add goes stale the moment they quit the app.

The proposal: register SMAppService.mainApp on first launch, surface the same Settings toggle so it is trivially reversible, and treat it as opt-out. macOS already backstops the user here -- a newly registered login item lands in .requiresApproval and appears in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, where they can kill it, and LaunchAtLoginToggle already renders that state.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE: this is roughly an hour of work that captures most of what the whole bluegull-aqi-hib epic (weeks) is trying to buy. hib.1's own KEY EQUIVALENCE note already establishes that Option 2 and Option 3 present the SAME user-visible permission surface -- one row in Login Items & Extensions, silently revocable. If that cost is paid either way, the cheap version should be tried and MEASURED before the expensive one is committed to. Recommend shipping this and observing for a week what freshness gap actually remains; that observation is a direct input to hib.1.

Does NOT fix bluegull-aqi-o3a (cache_delete terminating the app mid-session) -- SMAppService.mainApp relaunches at login, not after a RunningBoard termination. Those are separate problems.

Counter-arguments worth weighing before doing it: auto-enrolling a user in a login item without asking is the kind of thing App Review and privacy-minded users notice (relevant to bluegull-aqi-fw4.4); and it makes the app resident, which raises the per-install backend fetch rate (relevant to bluegull-aqi-q9r.36's still-disabled reserved concurrency). A first-run prompt rather than a silent register is the middle path.
acceptance_criteria: Steve makes the call. If yes: first launch registers mainApp, the Settings toggle reflects and can reverse it, .requiresApproval is surfaced, and the behavior is noted in ReleaseNotes.md. If no: record why on this issue and close.

title: SystemLocationProvider.requestLocation() has no timeout -- continuation can hang forever
description:
LocationResolver.swift's LocationRequestDelegate resumes its CheckedContinuation ONLY from didUpdateLocations (line 123) or didFailWithError (line 129). CLLocationManager.requestLocation() is not contractually guaranteed to deliver either promptly, and in practice can go quiet (no fix obtainable, location services wedged, Wi-Fi positioning unavailable with no GPS). When that happens currentLocation() never returns and never throws.

In the long-lived menu bar app this is an invisible hang in one refresh cycle -- bad but survivable, since the next cycle constructs a new provider.

It becomes severe for anything short-lived. Found while reviewing bluegull-aqi-hib: a launchd-started helper holds a transaction while it works, so a wedged continuation means the process NEVER EXITS -- which would destroy the "starts when needed, exits when idle" property that is the entire justification for the helper design over a resident app.

Fix: bound the wait (a Task-based timeout, or the CoreLocation error path plus a watchdog), call manager.stopUpdatingLocation() on timeout, and guard the continuation against double-resume -- the delegate already nils `continuation` after resuming, so the timeout path must go through that same guard rather than hold a second reference.

Sibling defect already tracked inside bluegull-aqi-hib.4: currentLocation() (LocationResolver.swift:100-102) throws .permissionDenied on .notDetermined without waiting for locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization. Same file, same short-lived-process exposure, different bug -- worth fixing together if either is picked up. Unlike hib.4 this one is NOT gated on the hib.1 go/no-go decision; it is a live defect in the shipping app.
acceptance_criteria: currentLocation() always completes (returns a value or throws) within a bounded time even when CoreLocation delivers no delegate callback at all. Covered by a unit test with a fake that never calls back.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-30 on branch feat/location-helper-agent.

Extracted a `LocationManaging` protocol (authorizationStatus / delegate / requestLocation / stopUpdatingLocation) with `CLLocationManager` conforming, so `SystemLocationProvider` takes an injectable manager and a `timeout` (default 15s, `SystemLocationProvider.defaultTimeout`). Every other system dependency in that file was already behind a protocol for testability; CLLocationManager was the one that wasn't, which is exactly why this shipped untested.

`LocationRequestDelegate` became `LocationRequest`, which now owns the continuation, the deadline, and a single NSLock-guarded `finish(with:)` that every outcome routes through -- fix, CoreLocation error, or timeout -- returning whether it won the race so a late arrival loses quietly instead of double-resuming (which traps on CheckedContinuation). The deadline is armed under the same lock acquisition that stores the continuation, so there is no window where a caller is suspended with nothing scheduled to wake it. On timeout, and only if the timeout won, `stopUpdatingLocation()` is called on the main queue (it is what cancels a pending one-shot requestLocation, and CLLocationManager wants a thread with a live run loop).

Added `LocationResolverError.timedOut(TimeInterval)` rather than reusing `.locationUnavailable("timed out")`. The distinction is the point of the bug: `.locationUnavailable` is CoreLocation actively reporting failure, `.timedOut` is silence. Confirmed no exhaustive switch over the enum anywhere in the app, widget, or kit, so adding the case broke nothing. Callers use `try?` (AQIRefreshController.swift:176,265) so app-visible behaviour is unchanged except that the call now actually completes.

7 tests in SystemLocationProviderTimeoutTests, all through a fake manager whose DEFAULT behaviour is the bug (accepts requestLocation, never says anything again): times out; cancels the pending request; an empty didUpdateLocations array still times out (the second silent hang path); a fix before the deadline wins and is NOT cancelled; a reported failure stays `.locationUnavailable` and does not get relabelled as silence; a late fix and a late error after the deadline are both discarded without a double-resume trap; and an unauthorized manager still fails fast without waiting out the deadline.

Full package suite 258/258 green, `make test-swift` green (app + widget targets build, BluegullAQITests pass).

NOT fixed here, still open inside hib.4: currentLocation() throws .permissionDenied on .notDetermined without waiting for locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization (LocationResolver.swift:100-102). Left alone deliberately -- it changes permission-flow behaviour in the shipping app, which is a bigger call than bounding a hang, and it is gated on the hib.1 decision.

title: Uninstall path: DMG script + in-app removal + stale window-frame fix
description:
Steve (2026-08-26/27): three related pieces of work, all about handling a real install's full lifecycle cleanup:

1. mac-app/scripts/uninstall.command -- a DMG-bundled uninstaller (double-click .command file) that removes the app bundle, both sandboxed containers (app + widget extension, plus a defensive check for a stray helper-agent container from an early hib-epic spike), the App Group shared data, the AirNow API key from Keychain, saved window state, crash logs, and LaunchServices registration. Wired into 'make app-package' (Makefile), with the DMG's window/background extended (mac-app/branding/gen-dmg-background.py, dmg-background.png) to give it its own row below the install instructions.

2. CompletelyRemoveButton.swift -- a 'Completely Remove BlueGull AQI...' button inside Settings itself, the PRIMARY/more discoverable uninstall path (Steve's own reasoning: most people delete the install DMG right after dragging the app to Applications, so a script that only lives there is invisible to anyone who wants to clean up later). Uses the proper UserDefaults/Keychain/SMAppService APIs (removePersistentDomain x2, AirNowAPIKeyStore.delete(), SMAppService.mainApp.unregister()) rather than raw filesystem removal on the app's own live sandbox container. Reveals the app in Finder and quits rather than self-deleting its own bundle.

3. SettingsWindowFrameSanitizer.swift -- fixes a real, live production issue Steve caught: anyone who installed a pre-a22 version and upgraded by just drag-replacing the app (the normal upgrade path -- nobody runs an uninstaller first) still carries that version's stale, oversized saved Settings-window frame (up to 1106pt wide) into the redesigned, much-narrower panel. Scrubbed from UserDefaults at app launch (BluegullAQIApp.init()), before any window is created, so there's no visible flash of the old layout. Went through several live-tested iterations: an initial version also checked window HEIGHT for staleness, which turned out to be a mistake -- confirmed live that a legitimately-grown Settings panel (1064pt tall with Direct mode + several pinned locations + the newer toggles/buttons added this session) got misjudged as 'stale' and force-repositioned, causing a visible flash of its own. Height was dropped from the staleness check entirely (a vertical VStack's height is EXPECTED to keep growing as features get added; width is the reliable signal since nothing in this layout grows it horizontally).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text: Implemented and confirmed live by Steve (2026-08-27). All three pieces working: uninstall.command wired into the DMG, CompletelyRemoveButton in Settings, and SettingsWindowFrameSanitizer fixing the real upgrade-path bug (confirmed via simulated stale-frame injection matching the exact real-world scenario: a pre-a22 1106pt-wide saved frame, scrubbed cleanly at launch with no flash). Also caught and fixed a self-inflicted regression during testing: an early version of the staleness check included a height cap that misfired on this panel's own legitimate growth (1064pt tall is correct now, not stale) -- removed height from the check entirely, kept width (the reliable signal) and the off-screen check.

Also close out two previously-filed bugs while touching this view: bluegull-aqi-e70.33 (Pinned Locations descriptive caption truncates instead of wrapping) and bluegull-aqi-e70.45 (Settings window too wide, caused by DataSourceModeToggle's full-sentence segmented-control labels).
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
Implemented and confirmed live by Steve (2026-08-25). Summary of the full arc, since this ended up touching more than the original scope:

BRANDING: Settings now uses AppBrand's gradient background, navy/white text matching the popover/detail window treatment (e70.51/e70.52), a shared `brandFieldStyle()` (white text on a filled midBlue box) for every TextField/SecureField, `.borderedProminent` buttons so their labels auto-contrast against the panel's `.tint(AppBrand.midBlue)`, and `.toggleStyle(.switch)` instead of the default checkbox style (the checkbox's dark checkmark glyph was hard to see against the gradient).

e70.33 (Pinned Locations caption truncating): fixed with `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)`, same established pattern as TimestampCaption/AttributionAndDisclaimerText.

e70.45 (Settings too wide): fixed by shortening DataSourceModeToggle's segmented labels to "Service"/"Direct" (was full sentences) and giving every TextField an explicit width instead of letting them size unconstrained.

Three additional real bugs found only through live testing, none caught by the render-without-crashing smoke tests:
1. A stale AppKit "NSWindow Frame settings" autosave entry (1106pt wide, from before this change) silently overrode every width fix until cleared via `defaults delete`. No code fix for an already-stale entry; `.defaultSize`/`.windowResizability(.contentSize)` only govern a window with no saved frame yet.
2. ScrollView + Spacer(): without `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)` on the scrolled content, each row's Spacer expanded toward an unbounded canvas instead of the ScrollView's real width, stretching fields and misplacing the trailing trash button.
3. On Steve's 3-display rig (built-in 2560x1664 + two external 1920x1200s), the Settings window kept opening off-screen -- `.defaultPosition(.center)`, `NSWindow.center()` ("most area" screen), and mouse-location-based centering were all tried and failed live. What worked: an explicit small inset from `NSScreen.main`'s own visibleFrame origin (SettingsView.swift's `.onAppear` handler). Also found: the Pinned Locations ScrollView's height must be a FIXED `.frame(height:)`, not just `.frame(maxHeight:)` -- with only a ceiling, the region sized itself off `locations.count` at the very first layout pass (before `.onAppear`'s `store.load()` populated the real list), and never grew again once the real 11-item list loaded, squeezing the list into a sliver. A constant height keeps SettingsView's own ideal size independent of how many pins exist.

11 pins show without a scrollbar; a 12th triggers it -- Steve confirmed close enough to the "~10 visible" spec, not worth tuning further.

All verified via make test-swift (full pass) and multiple live rebuild+relaunch cycles.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
Confirmed live by Steve (2026-08-25): "AQI" label reads well on all three widget sizes once the stale widget extension process was cleared.

Found a real repro of a previously-diagnosed class of issue in this session: `ps aux` showed the running BluegullAQIWidget.appex process had started at 10:45 AM, hours before this change's rebuilt binary (timestamped 15:40) -- the widget host doesn't restart its extension process just because the underlying binary changed on disk, so the desktop widgets kept rendering the old code after a normal `make app-run`. `kill`ing that PID alone didn't trigger an immediate respawn (WidgetKit only relaunches on its own schedule/next timeline reload). `pkill -x NotificationCenter` (the desktop widget host on macOS) forced an immediate fresh extension process, timestamped after the rebuild, and the new "AQI" label appeared right away.

Not a code bug -- no production or test code changed for this. Noting it here since it's the second time in this session `make app-run`/`make widget-reset` alone wasn't enough to see a widget change live; `make widget-reset`'s own LaunchServices-registration fix is a different failure mode from this one (stale registration vs. stale already-running process), so both are worth knowing about when a widget change doesn't show up after a rebuild.

title: Extend branded gradient to the popover and widget detail window
description:
Steve, 2026-08-25: "Now let's give the popover and detail panels a similar
treatment. Consistency is good!" -- extending bluegull-aqi-e70.51's widget-
face branding (icon-blue-to-navy gradient, real EPA scale bar) to
AQIPopoverView and WidgetDetailView.

New AppBrand.swift (mac-app/BluegullAQI/) -- a deliberate duplicate of
BluegullAQIWidgetViews' WidgetBrand, not a cross-module import, matching
this codebase's own established "each UI target converts/defines brand
color code at its own point of use" precedent (AQIColor+SwiftUI.swift is
already duplicated the same way between these two targets).

Real design difference from the widget faces, worth recording: content
height in these two views varies a lot (empty/error state vs. a full
pollutant list plus timestamps plus the attribution paragraph) and
WidgetDetailView SCROLLS -- unlike the fixed-size, non-scrolling widget
faces. Text colors in this file are chosen PER ELEMENT (navy near the top,
white elsewhere), so the gradient has to move WITH whichever element it's
behind:
- AQIPopoverView has no ScrollView, so a single `.background()` behind the
  whole VStack works exactly like the widget faces did.
- WidgetDetailView's gradient lives INSIDE the ScrollView, behind the
  content VStack (sized to the content's own height), NOT behind the
  ScrollView container itself -- a background fixed to the window would
  stay in place while the user scrolls content over it, eventually putting
  white-colored (normally-lower) content over the still-light top on
  scroll. Also added a solid-navy (not a second gradient) fallback behind
  the ScrollView for when this resizable, frame-persisted window is taller
  than its content -- a flat color can't produce the seam a second
  *gradient* layer did on the widget faces (e70.51's real bug, fixed there
  by removing the second layer, not by adding a matching flat one).

Two things NOT independently confirmed live yet, flagged in code comments
at their call sites -- worth a specific look, not just the general
live-check every UI change here gets:
- MenuBarLocationPicker (a stock `.menu`-style Picker) -- tried `.tint`,
  since `.foregroundStyle` is documented not to reliably reach a Picker's
  own label text on that style, but unconfirmed whether it actually shows
  up against the new background.
- ContentUnavailableView (stock SwiftUI type, used for empty/error states
  in both views) -- chained `.foregroundStyle(.white)` as a best-effort;
  unconfirmed whether that actually recolors its internal title AND
  description, or just one, or neither.

No pixel-golden tests exist for these two views (only render-without-
crashing smoke tests, confirmed by direct check before starting) -- this
change carries no golden-image re-recording cost, unlike e70.51's widget
work.

title: Redesign widget faces: branded background + AQI scale bar (all 3 sizes)
description:
Design canvas: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/89fd3628-000e-4071-b65b-3a8eb37f2263
(2 directions explored for Small; scale-bar direction chosen and extended to
Medium/Large. Radial-gauge alternate kept on the canvas, archived/not pursued.)

Steve, 2026-08-25: "The AQI widget faces could use some more pizzazz. Blue
Gull background color as branding. A scale of the category colors as well
as indicating where the current observation is." Then: "I was hoping to use
the much lighter blue from the background of the Blue Gull AQI icon. Fine
to make that a gradient to a darker blue in the brand palette." Then: "I
like the scale bar design... now do something similar for the other size
widgets."

## Design, as approved

All three widget sizes (SmallWidgetLayout/MediumWidgetLayout/
LargeWidgetLayout, BluegullAQIWidgetView.swift):

- Background: replaces the current `.containerBackground(.background, for:
  .widget)` (plain adaptive system background) with a branded gradient --
  the app icon's own light blue (ARROW_BLUE, #70B5EC / RGB 112,181,236,
  per mac-app/branding/gen-dmg-background.py and branding/README.md) at
  the top, fading through a mid-blue to the brand navy (#142846 / RGB
  20,40,70, same source) at the bottom.
- Text color: location name + resolved place name (top, over the lighter
  part of the gradient) switch from adaptive `.secondary` to a fixed navy;
  everything else (AQI number, category descriptor, pollutant names,
  aged-reading caption, dividers) switches from adaptive `.primary`/
  `.secondary` to fixed white/white-opacity, since the background is no
  longer the adaptive system one. Small's stale-badge icon (top-right,
  over the light zone) also goes navy; Medium/Large's aged-reading row
  (bottom, over the dark zone) stays white.
- The small colored `Circle()` category dot (all 3 layouts) is replaced by
  a horizontal scale-bar: a rounded pill with 6 hard-stop color segments
  (the real EPA category colors from AQICategory.color, at fractions
  0-0.15-0.30-0.45-0.60-0.85-1.0 -- deliberately NOT proportional to AQI
  point-range above 300, compressing Very Unhealthy/Hazardous so all 6
  colors stay visible on a small bar) and a white/navy-bordered marker
  circle positioned at the current reading's fraction along it.
- Pollutant AQI badges (Medium/Large's colored-background pill treatment)
  are UNCHANGED -- already self-contained, no legibility issue against the
  new background.
- Dividers (Medium/Large, currently plain SwiftUI `Divider()`) need to
  become an explicit white/~28%-opacity hairline -- the default `Divider()`
  renders as system adaptive gray, which won't read against the new
  background.

## Implementation notes (not yet built)

- New shared logic, BluegullAQIKit (not BluegullAQIWidgetViews -- pure
  data, reusable): the aqi-to-scale-fraction piecewise mapping. Do NOT
  duplicate AQICategory's own breakpoints for category lookup -- the
  layouts already receive `category: AQICategory` directly; only the
  *scale position* (fraction 0...1) is new.
  - Design canvas breakpoint table (aqi -> fraction): 0->0, 50->0.15,
    100->0.30, 150->0.45, 200->0.60, 300->0.85, 500->1.0, piecewise linear
    between, clamped to [0,500] before mapping.
- New shared view, BluegullAQIWidgetViews (reuses AQIColor/AQICategory,
  same module SmallWidgetLayout etc. already live in): the scale-bar-plus-
  marker component, parameterized by width/height so Small/Medium/Large
  can each size it appropriately (mockup: Small ~128pt, Medium ~128pt in
  its narrower left column, Large full-width ~300pt).
- Brand colors (#70B5EC / #142846, and a blended mid-stop) need their own
  home -- likely a small new file in BluegullAQIWidgetViews, same
  duplication-with-cross-reference-comment precedent as AQIColor+SwiftUI.swift
  (that type is deliberately duplicated between BluegullAQIWidgetViews and
  the BluegullAQI app target rather than shared via BluegullAQIKit, which
  has no UI framework dependency by design) -- these are widget-only for
  now per this bead's scope, not applied to the menu bar popover.

  Medium mockups (48%) and Large mockup (30%, transitioning to navy sooner

- `BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests` golden images will all need

  BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests`, reviewed as always per that command's

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
Implemented 2026-08-25 (commit ed7434a). All three widget sizes now use the
approved design: WidgetBrand.backgroundGradient (icon-blue #70B5EC -> navy
#142846) and AQIScaleBar (six EPA category colors, marker via the new
AQIScale.fraction(forAQI:)) replace the old plain background and dot in
SmallWidgetLayout/MediumWidgetLayout/LargeWidgetLayout.

Real bug found and fixed along the way, not just a style change: the
straightforward `.containerBackground(for: .widget) { customGradient }`
approach silently rendered NOTHING under the headless snapshot-test harness
-- a golden image came back with no gradient at all and the new white text
invisible against the harness's plain white canvas. Root cause: that
view-builder overload needs a real WidgetKit container behind it to
actually render the closure's content, which WidgetRenderHarness's bare
ImageRenderer doesn't provide. Fixed by painting the gradient as an
ordinary `.background()` (works identically in the harness and on a real
host) while keeping the separate, already-proven-working
`.containerBackground(.background, for: .widget)` call for WidgetKit's own
requirement that it be called at all. Confirmed this fix by actually
looking at the re-recorded golden images, not just re-running the tests --
the first recording attempt visibly had the bug (plain white background,
missing AQI number/category text), the second (after the fix) didn't.

Also hit and fixed a real false-positive in ComplianceTests
.testNoAQIDerivationLogicExistsInSources -- its naive substring scan
flagged the words "breakpoint" and "interpolat" in AQIScale.swift's own
comments/identifiers as looking like forbidden concentration-to-AQI
derivation logic (bluegull-aqi-10h.17), even though the code only maps an
already-AirNow-supplied AQI integer to a scale position, never derives an
AQI value itself. Fixed by rewording the new file, not by touching the
compliance guard, which is guarding something real.

Verified: full test-swift green (BluegullAQIKit + BluegullAQITests), new
AQIScaleTests (5 tests: exact breakpoints, mid-band interpolation, clamping
above 500 and below 0, monotonicity), all 17 widget snapshot goldens
re-recorded and individually reviewed by eye (not just re-run) -- confirmed
dark-mode variants now render identically to light mode (background is
deliberately fixed, not adaptive -- expected), marker clamps correctly at
both AQI extremes (5 and 500), empty/stale states stay legible in white on
the gradient.

Rebuilt and relaunched the dev app (make app-run) so this can be checked
live against the real widget host -- not yet confirmed live by Steve
(snapshot-test/ImageRenderer review only so far, which is exactly the kind
of headless-vs-real-host gap this bead's own containerBackground bug came

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
Follow-up fix, 2026-08-25 (commit 56d4f0b): found live on Steve's actual
desktop -- a visible white border around the branded content, because
.background() only fills the content's own layout bounds, not WidgetKit's
reserved margin around it, which the plain
.containerBackground(.background, for: .widget) call was still painting
with the system background. The snapshot harness genuinely can't catch
this class of bug: it has no concept of WidgetKit's margin at all, so all
17 goldens stayed green through this the whole time. Fixed by also calling
.containerBackground(for: .widget) { gradient } (the real API for
extending into that margin) alongside the existing .background() (kept
for the harness, which still doesn't render that closure's content).

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
Second follow-up fix, 2026-08-25 (commit bf5c518): the white-border fix
itself (comment above) introduced a NEW visible defect -- a rectangular
seam right where the content region's edge met the surrounding margin.

painting the "same" gradient, they're actually painted over two
DIFFERENT-sized views (content's own layout bounds vs the full
margin-inclusive canvas), so a percentage-based gradient's stops land at

not a seamless fill, on a real host.

exactly ONE background call: .containerBackground(for:)) and into the

testLargeTypicalDarkMode, WidgetRenderHarness's fixture loop). WidgetBrand
made public so the non-@testable WidgetRenderHarness target can reach it.

All 17 goldens re-recorded -- pixel-identical in appearance to the
previous (seamed) recording, since the fix is specifically about
