title: Air Quality Detail window freezes its reading on open -- never refreshes while left open, diverging from the live menu bar
description:
Steve (2026-08-24): observed the menu bar showing AQI 42 while the "Air Quality Detail" window (opened via a placed widget's tap target) showed 52, at the same time. Originally filed as "desire, not sure it's a requirement" pending investigation -- investigation (below) found a concrete, source-confirmed bug, not just an inherent architectural tradeoff, so this is now a real fix candidate.

## Root cause (confirmed by reading the source, 2026-08-24)

`WidgetDetailView`'s `reading`/`freshness` are plain `@State`, populated exactly once by `.task(id: location)` (mac-app/BluegullAQI/WidgetDetailView.swift:148-153):

    .task(id: location) {
        refreshFromCache()
        guard reading == nil else { return }
        await refreshController?.fetchIfNeeded(for: location)
        refreshFromCache()
    }

`fetchIfNeeded` (mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQIRefreshController.swift:260-274) only fetches on an actual cache miss (`guard ... cache.get(for: resolvedLocation.rounded) == nil else { return }`, line 269) -- so once the shared cache has *anything* for this location, the guard at WidgetDetailView.swift:150 skips fetching entirely.

Net effect: **once this window has loaded a reading, nothing ever refreshes it again while the window stays open.** No timer, no observer on the shared App Group cache, no link to `refreshController`'s own live state. It's a singleton `Window` (id "widget-detail", declared in mac-app/BluegullAQI/BluegullAQIApp.swift:144-149), so it's easy to leave open indefinitely.

Contrast with the menu bar/popover, which both read `refreshController.latestReading` directly (BluegullAQIApp.swift:98, 116) -- an `@Observable` property that updates live every time the app's own background fetch loop succeeds.

So: open the detail window, leave it open, let the app's background loop successfully fetch one or more times -- the menu bar climbs/moves to whatever's current, the open detail window stays frozen at whatever it showed at open time. Since AQI isn't monotonic, either view can end up looking "ahead" of the other; there's no inherent direction to the discrepancy.

**This day's timeline is consistent with that**: process running since 2026-08-23 13:14 (yesterday). A real 502 hit at 09:30:38 this morning, auto-retried 62s later per bluegull-aqi-e70.47's new backoff (succeeded 09:31:46 -- good real-world confirmation that fix works), then fetched again normally at 10:30:28. If the detail window was already open across either of those successful fetches, the menu bar would have moved on while the window didn't -- matching what Steve saw, and matching it resolving itself ("up until a few minutes ago") once the window was presumably closed/reopened, which re-runs `.task(id:)`.

## Secondary, lower-confidence consideration (not confirmed today, worth keeping in mind)

If the tapped widget is pinned to a location OTHER than "Current Location" (e.g. a specific named pin, cached under its own rounded coordinates), that cache bucket is written by a genuinely separate fetch loop -- the widget extension's own independent per-widget fetching (moved there in bluegull-aqi-mtm.24) -- on its own schedule, distinct from both the container app's menu-bar-selection fetch and its "keep Current Location warm" sub-fetch (AQIRefreshController.swift:14-29). Two different real-world fetch times for two different processes CAN legitimately produce two different-but-both-correct-at-their-own-moment values even with the primary bug above fixed. Not the mechanism behind today's specific observation (that was traced to the frozen-@State issue above), but worth a sentence in the fix's design notes so it isn't rediscovered fresh later.

## Suggested fix direction

Give `WidgetDetailView` a way to notice a newer cache write while it's open -- simplest version: also refresh on window activation/foreground (SwiftUI's `.onAppear` won't refire for an already-visible singleton Window across focus changes; likely needs `NSWindow`-level active/`ScenePhase`-style observation, or reusing whatever the menu bar popover uses to know its own data changed, since that one visibly does stay live). Alternatively, poll `refreshFromCache()` on a lightweight timer while the window is key/visible. Needs a real design decision, not just "add a timer" -- confirm approach before implementing.

## Real-world confirmation (2026-08-24 ~16:35)

Left the "Air Quality Detail" window open continuously in a dev build (launched 13:51, no restarts) across two independent live AirNow-502 outage/backoff-recovery cycles (14:30-14:33, 15:30-15:33) plus a normal-cadence fetch at 16:30 -- confirmed via unified log (CFNetwork task summaries), not guessed. Response body size shifted 979 -> 976 bytes between the early and later successful fetches, confirming the underlying reading actually changed, not just repeated fetches of identical data. At the end of that window, menu bar and detail panel values were compared side by side and matched. The exact menu-bar-42/detail-52 divergence this bead was filed for did not recur across multiple real opportunities to go stale.
acceptance_criteria: WidgetDetailView's displayed reading/freshness stays in sync with the shared App Group cache while the window remains open, matching what the menu bar/popover show for the same location -- not just at open time. Covered by a test that: opens the view, simulates a subsequent successful fetch updating the cache for the same location, and asserts the view's displayed reading updates without the window being closed/reopened. Design for HOW to detect the update (foreground/activation hook vs. lightweight polling vs. a proper live observer) decided and documented before implementation, not assumed.
close_reason: Fixed with the Darwin-notification approach (design confirmed with Steve, preferring correctness over a polling/activation-only workaround given the race-condition risk). New CacheChangeBroadcast.swift in BluegullAQIKit: UserDefaultsCacheStore.set posts a Darwin notification (bridged to NotificationCenter.default, since the C callback can't capture context) after every real write -- the one path both the container app and widget extension go through. WidgetDetailView now consumes CacheChangeObserving.changes() inside its existing .task(id: location) block (not a second modifier), so a location change correctly cancels and restarts the subscription the same way it already does the fetch-on-open logic. Injectable (CacheChangeObserving protocol + DarwinCacheChangeObserver/ManualCacheChangeObserver fake) matching this package's established real-vs-fake pattern. Full test-swift green, 229/229 (6 new: CacheChangeBroadcastTests exercises the real Darwin round-trip including that cancellation actually tears down the observer, not just stops consuming; UserDefaultsCacheStoreTests confirms both the write and the removal branch of set() broadcast). Honest gap: this covers the underlying broadcast mechanism at the BluegullAQIKit level, matching how this codebase already tests OS-glue (real API, not just a fake, per UserDefaultsCacheStoreTests' own doc comment) -- WidgetDetailView's own consumption wiring is thin and not independently unit-tested (this project doesn't have SwiftUI-view-level test tooling), same treatment as AQIRefreshController and other thin app-level wrappers. Real-world confirmation (open the Air Quality Detail window, leave it open across a fetch cycle, watch it update live) not yet done -- worth a quick manual check next time the app is running.

title: Both detail panels (menu bar popover + widget detail window) show observation time AND update time, identically formatted, always visible
description:
Steve (2026-08-23, refining the same-day request this bead was filed for): this should appear on BOTH detail panels, not just the widget one -- the menu bar popover (AQIPopoverView) and the widget detail window (WidgetDetailView) are the two panels meant. General spec: both detail panels should show the same last-update information in the same way -- one shared format/component, not two independently-formatted ones.

Steve also confirmed directly: the widget detail panel currently shows NO update time at all for a fresh reading -- confirms the "always shown vs. stale-only" open question below is resolved: show it unconditionally, not gated on freshness.

## Current state (two panels, two different formats, both wrong per the new spec)

**Menu bar popover** -- mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQIPopoverView.swift:110-111 calls updatedCaption(lastFetchedAt) (defined 169-176): Text("Updated ") + Text(date, style: .relative), live-updating, relative-only ("Updated 2 hours ago"), shown whenever lastFetchedAt is present (line 44's AQIRefreshController.lastFetchedAt -- FETCH time, not observation time). No absolute date/time/timezone, no seconds.

**Widget detail window** -- mac-app/BluegullAQI/WidgetDetailView.swift:123-125: if freshness == .stale { AgedReadingIndicator(headline: headline) }. AgedReadingIndicator (mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQISummaryComponents.swift:79-94) renders PollutantReading.observedAtDisplay (mac-app/BluegullAQIKit/Sources/BluegullAQIKit/PollutantReading+Observation.swift:52-59): DateFormatter "EEE MMM d, h:mm a zzz" -- absolute, minute resolution, reporting-station's own timezone (OBSERVATION time, not fetch time) -- but ONLY rendered when stale. Nothing shown at all for a fresh reading, which is what Steve observed.

## New unified spec (both panels, identical)

Absolute date + time + timezone at 1-second resolution, with the relative time in parentheses to the right, shown unconditionally (fresh or stale) -- e.g. "Tue Aug 12, 2026, 5:00:00 PM EDT (2 hours ago)". Suggests factoring this into one shared SwiftUI component both AQIPopoverView and WidgetDetailView use, rather than each view formatting it independently the way they do today (this is exactly how the two diverged into different formats in the first place -- see AQISummaryComponents.swift's existing role as the shared-component home for both surfaces, e.g. AgedReadingIndicator and AQIHeadlineBadge already live there).

## Which timestamp: BOTH (resolved, 2026-08-23)

Steve: "it would be useful to show both the observation time and the update time on the detail panels." So both panels show two timestamps, each in the same absolute-date/time/timezone-at-1s + relative-in-parens format:

- **Observation time** -- AirNow's own reported observation timestamp (reporting station's own timezone), what PollutantReading.observedAtDisplay already sources (mac-app/BluegullAQIKit/Sources/BluegullAQIKit/PollutantReading+Observation.swift:52-59), just currently formatted at minute resolution with no relative suffix.
- **Update time** -- when this app last successfully fetched/cached the reading (viewer's own local timezone), i.e. AQIRefreshController.lastFetchedAt (mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQIRefreshController.swift:48) on the popover side; WidgetDetailView doesn't currently track a fetch-time equivalent at all (only observedAtDisplay via AgedReadingIndicator) -- will need to be threaded through/exposed there too, likely via WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot's existing lastSuccessfulFetchDate (see WidgetTimelineComputerTests' testCurrentSnapshotLastSuccessfulFetchDateIsNilWhenNeverFetched / ...SurfacesLastSuccessfulFetchDateEvenOnceTheEntryHasExpired for where that value already exists in the widget's data model).

These two can genuinely differ (e.g. AirNow's own station observation lags real-world time by its own publish cadence, independent of when *this app* last fetched it) -- showing both, clearly labeled, avoids papering over that distinction rather than picking one arbitrarily.

## Other open questions still needing a decision before/during implementation

- This reverses bluegull-aqi-e70.31's scope decision, which explicitly said "the popover is a separate surface... should probably keep doing so" (i.e. stay relative-only forever) -- flagging so whoever implements this doesn't get confused finding that closed issue's opposite conclusion. e70.31 was about the bare menu-bar status item (hide the number once stale), NOT the popover's caption -- worth rereading e70.31's own text before assuming this bead conflicts with it; it may only have been describing the *status item*, with the popover's own relative caption being incidental, unexamined, and not itself a deliberate "keep it relative" ruling. Confirm the actual scope of e70.31's decision before treating this as an intentional reversal vs. just filling a gap nobody looked at closely.
acceptance_criteria: Both mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQIPopoverView.swift and mac-app/BluegullAQI/WidgetDetailView.swift show TWO timestamps -- observation time and update/fetch time, each clearly labeled -- via one shared component (e.g. added to AQISummaryComponents.swift) with identical formatting: absolute date + time + timezone at 1-second resolution, plus a live-updating relative-time string in parentheses to the right. Shown unconditionally in both panels (not gated on freshness/staleness). WidgetDetailView gains access to a fetch-time value it doesn't currently expose (likely via WidgetTimelineComputer's existing lastSuccessfulFetchDate). Covered by tests verifying the shared component's format/precision and that both call sites use it for both timestamps.
close_reason: Implemented -- both detail panels show unified observation + update timestamps via shared TimestampCaption component. See comment for full details and one open follow-up (live layout check).

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
Implemented 2026-08-24 (commit 6e0d38b). Both AQIPopoverView and
WidgetDetailView now show two unconditional timestamps via one new shared

absolute date/time/timezone at 1-second resolution + live-updating relative

title: AirNow API times out around :30 past the hour, causing hourly fetch failures
description:
Dev backend Lambda (bluegull-aqi-dev-AqiFunction) intermittently times out calling AirNow's API (10s budget in airnow_client.py) specifically for requests clustered around :30 past the hour. Confirmed 2026-08-22: this install's fetches (its RefreshScheduler install-offset phase lands at ~30m23s into each hour) failed with AirNow timeouts at 10:30, 12:30, 13:30, and 14:30 local, while other dev-backend installs polling the same location at different offsets (~:41-42 past the hour) succeeded in the same windows with normal (~1-2s) AirNow response times. Not a Bluegull backend bug -- the Lambda logs show it faithfully waiting out its own 10s timeout and returning cleanly; AirNow itself just isn't answering within that budget during this window.

## Context
Diagnosed via: client-side unified log (log show) correlated against CloudWatch logs for bluegull-aqi-dev-AqiFunction, cross-referenced with the shared App Group cache's own last-successful/last-failed timestamps on the affected Mac. See bluegull-aqi-e70.47 for the client-side mitigation (fast-retry backoff) -- that reduces user-visible impact but doesn't address the root cause here, which is external (AirNow).

title: Fast retry after a transient fetch failure, before falling back to hourly cadence
description:
AQIRefreshController.runLoop() (mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQIRefreshController.swift:131) retries on RefreshScheduler's fixed per-install hourly cadence regardless of whether the last fetch succeeded or failed -- there is no faster backoff-and-retry for a transient error. Steve saw the container app's menu bar (and any widget depending on its Current Location cache slot) stop updating after real 502/503s from the service backend, recovering only once he changed the menu bar's location, which triggers an out-of-band refreshNow() (BluegullAQIApp.swift:101) that happens to succeed once the backend has recovered. Investigation found no circuit breaker or negative caching in AppGroupCache.recordFailedFetch() -- the loop was always going to retry, just not for up to an hour, since AWS 502/503 bursts (Lambda cold start, ALB hiccup) are typically far shorter than that.

## Context
Investigated 2026-08-19: read AQIRefreshController.swift, RefreshScheduler.swift, AQIFetchCoordinator.swift, AppGroupCache.swift, BluegullServiceClient.swift, BluegullAQIWidget.swift. Confirmed no backoff/circuit-breaker exists anywhere; RefreshScheduler.nextRefreshDate() is a fixed install-offset hourly schedule with no awareness of fetch outcome. Separately flagged (not filed as a bead yet): this app is LSUIElement with no ProcessInfo.beginActivity() App Nap opt-out, which may compound the perceived stall by suspending the background timer loop itself -- worth checking Activity Monitor/Console for App Nap during a real stall before assuming this bead's fix alone explains the full symptom.
acceptance_criteria: On a fetch failure, the next retry happens on a short bounded schedule (e.g. a handful of attempts a minute or so apart) instead of waiting for the next hourly slot; once those short retries are exhausted (or one succeeds), falls back to the normal RefreshScheduler cadence. Covered by a unit test in BluegullAQIKitTests exercising the retry timing, not just a manual check.
close_reason: Implemented as exponential backoff (60s, 120s, then held at a 240s cap) across up to 6 attempts (~19 minutes total) before falling back to the normal hourly cadence -- covers the ~11-12 minute AirNow recovery window measured live 2026-08-22 (see bluegull-aqi-bkv for that investigation), not just the originally-assumed 'well under a minute' AWS blip. RefreshScheduler.nextRefreshDate(consecutiveFailures:) and AQIRefreshController wired up; covered by RefreshSchedulerTests. Full test-swift green.

title: Menu bar AQI label disappears in stale/unavailable fallback states
description:
Tester feedback (pre-release 0.1.0 direct build, 2026-08-19): the optional 'AQI' menu bar label (bluegull-aqi-e70.29, toggle off by default) should appear whenever it's enabled, not only when a fresh value is available -- it should still show for the stale-reading fallback (icon + em dash) and the never-fetched fallback (icon only), e.g. 'AQI —', not just a bare dash or bare icon.

Root cause: MenuBarStatusLabel.body (mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQISummaryComponents.swift) only calls the labelText(aqi:) helper -- which prepends 'AQI ' per the isAQILabelEnabled toggle -- from the fresh-value branch. The two fallback branches (freshness != .fresh / lastError != nil, and reading == nil) render a bare Image+Text("—") or bare Image, bypassing labelText entirely, so the toggle has no effect in those states.

Fix should extend the label-aware rendering to both fallback branches, respecting isAQILabelEnabled, consistent with e70.29's 'AQI' before value convention.

title: Configurable per-source request timeout, tab-style Settings for the selected source
description:
Steve (2026-08-18): 'we've exceeded our client response timeout to the lambda on cold starts on occasion. I think it was 10 seconds. Let's increase that to 15 seconds and see how it goes. Second, let's make that timeout a configureable setting. I believe we should have a timeout settable per data source. Third, this means that Service will now have a configuration section. Therefore, let's treat the source selection as if they were tabs to expose the settings for the selected source and only the selected source.'

Design decisions from AskUserQuestion:
- Service's default bumped 10s -> 15s; Direct stays at 10s (unaffected by the Lambda cold-start problem this exists for).
- Stored in the App Group (RequestTimeoutStore), not container-app-only -- both AirNowDirectClient and BluegullServiceClient are used by the widget extension's own fetches too.
- Stepper control (5s increments, 5-60s range), not a free-form text field.
- API key field now fully hidden outside Direct mode (pure tab semantics), not shown-but-disabled as e70.30 originally had it.
acceptance_criteria: RequestTimeoutStore (new, App Group-backed) exposes directTimeout(in:)/serviceTimeout(in:), read fresh on every request by both clients (matching e70.28's dev-URL-override precedent, not captured once at init). SettingsView's DataSourceModeToggle acts as a tab selector: only the selected mode's section renders below it (Direct: API key field + DirectTimeoutStepper; Service: explanatory text + ServiceTimeoutStepper).
close_reason: RequestTimeoutStore (App Group-backed, mirrors DataSourceModeStore) added with per-source directTimeout/serviceTimeout, resolved fresh per-request in both clients. Service default bumped to 15s. SettingsView restructured so DataSourceModeToggle acts as a tab selector -- API key field + its own timeout stepper only under Direct, explanatory text + timeout stepper only under Service. All layers tested: RequestTimeoutStoreTests, client-level timeout-applied tests, UI tests for tab-scoped visibility. Build + full test-swift green.

title: Air Quality Detail popup has no staleness indication at all
description:
Steve, confirming e70.39/e70.41's widget fix worked: 'The widget has the stale (clock) indicator now. Still displays the value. I think that's working as designed. Not that the Air Quality Detail popup has no indication of staleness at all, which is no bueno.'

WidgetDetailView only ever read .reading from WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot(for:) -- it discarded .freshness entirely, so tapping through to the detail window showed a reading with zero indication it might be aged, or that the active data source might be currently failing (freshness already folds bluegull-aqi-e70.39's cross-process failure signal in, via WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot -- WidgetDetailView just never looked at it).
acceptance_criteria: WidgetDetailView tracks freshness alongside reading and shows a new shared AgedReadingIndicator (clock-badge icon + absolute observation timestamp, matching the widget faces' own dc2.6/dc2.7 visual language) when freshness == .stale.
close_reason: WidgetDetailView now tracks freshness and shows a shared AgedReadingIndicator (clock-badge icon + absolute observation time) when stale, matching the widget faces' own visual language. Automatically inherits e70.39's cross-process failure signal too, since both read the same WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot. Tests added, all green.

title: Menu bar never nudges WidgetKit to reload on a failed fetch
acceptance_criteria: AQIRefreshController.refreshNow()'s catch let error as AQIFetchError branch also calls WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines(ofKind: BluegullWidgetKind.aqi), matching the success branch.
close_reason: Added the missing WidgetCenter.shared.reloadTimelines() call to the failure branch, matching the success branch. Confirmed live: AppGroupCache's failure signal was already correct, this was the missing nudge.

title: Popover error banner truncates instead of wrapping; shorten Service-mode error wording
description:
Steve, testing e70.38's improved Service-mode error message: 'The popover shows a more specific error, but sadly I can't read it, as it is right-truncated rather than wrapped!' AQIPopoverView.staleWarningBanner's Label had no wrap/fixedSize modifier -- Text/Label don't grow vertically inside a VStack on their own, so a longer message just clipped with an ellipsis.

Also, separately: 'Bluegull shared service reported a problem' is verbose. 'Service error:' would be fine -- shortened AQIFetchError.serviceModeError's message prefix and per-case failure descriptions to fit that shorter 'Service error: <reason>' format.
acceptance_criteria: staleWarningBanner gets .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true) so it wraps instead of truncating. serviceModeError's message reads 'Service error: <reason>. Try again shortly, or switch to Direct mode...' instead of 'BlueGull's shared service <reason>...'
close_reason: staleWarningBanner now wraps via fixedSize; serviceModeError's message shortened to 'Service error: <reason>' format. Build + tests green.

title: Widgets show no indication when the active fetch is failing
description:
Follow-up to bluegull-aqi-e70.37 (menu bar fix). Steve, same test session: "the widgets still show that the data is fresh." Root cause: widget freshness (AppGroupCache.freshness(for:)) is purely TTL-based, with zero concept of whether the most recent fetch ATTEMPT succeeded or failed. A Current Location widget never fetches for itself at all (no location entitlement in the extension) -- it's entirely dependent on whatever the container app last wrote to the shared cache, so it has no local signal whatsoever to know the active data source just started failing. A pinned-location widget does attempt its own fetch on cache miss, but swallows failures silently (try?) with nothing recorded anywhere.

Steve picked the design: a global (not per-location) 'last fetch attempt failed' flag, reusing the existing aged-reading badge/caption treatment (dc2.5/dc2.6) rather than a new visual. Accepted tradeoff: since it's global, a failure fetching one location could occasionally flag a widget whose own location is actually fine, or vice versa -- matches the existing precedent of lastFetchedAt/lastSuccessfulFetchDate already being global for the same reason.
acceptance_criteria: AppGroupCache gains recordFailedFetch/lastFailedFetchDate/isMostRecentFetchAttemptFailing, mirroring the existing recordSuccessfulFetch/lastSuccessfulFetchDate pair. AQIFetchCoordinator's fetchDirect/fetchService call cache.recordFailedFetch() on every AirNowError catch -- one choke point covering every caller in both processes, not scattered per call site. WidgetTimelineComputer.currentSnapshot downgrades .fresh to .stale when isMostRecentFetchAttemptFailing() is true, so widgets reuse the existing aged-reading treatment instead of showing nothing.
close_reason: AppGroupCache now tracks a global last-failed-fetch timestamp symmetric to its existing last-succeeded one; AQIFetchCoordinator records into it from a single choke point covering every caller; WidgetTimelineComputer downgrades a technically-fresh reading to .stale when the most recent attempt failed, reusing the existing aged-reading UI. Tests added at all three layers, all green.

title: Service-mode errors said 'Unknown error' and leaked AirNow-specific wording
description:
Steve's report (2026-08-18), disabling the service and switching to Service mode: the popover's stale-warning banner showed 'Unknown error.' His complaint, verbatim: "'Unknown error' usually means something we cannot anticipate, and the service not responding or otherwise telling us it's not available is hardly unexpected! Sloppy software engineering."

Root causes, two of them:
1. BluegullServiceClient.errorForFailedResponse fell back to the literal string 'Unknown error' whenever a non-2xx response body didn't parse as lambda_handler.py's own {"error": "..."} contract (e.g. API Gateway's own throttling/gateway-error responses, which never reach the handler).
2. AQIFetchCoordinator.fetchService wrapped every non-429 failure as the shared .airNowError case, whose userMessage says 'AirNow' throughout -- accurate for Direct mode (AirNowDirectClient really does talk to AirNow) but misleading for Service mode, which talks to our own backend.
acceptance_criteria: New AQIFetchError.serviceModeError(AirNowError) case builds its own Service-mode-accurate message from the underlying AirNowError's shape (network failure / HTTP status / decode failure), never says 'Unknown error' or 'AirNow', and still nudges toward Direct mode. BluegullServiceClient's raw fallback message is now 'No error details in response body' instead of 'Unknown error'.
close_reason: New AQIFetchError.serviceModeError case builds an honest, Service-mode-accurate message from the failure shape itself, never 'Unknown error' or 'AirNow' wording. Tests added covering both the message-quality assertions and the underlying client's raw fallback text.

title: Menu bar shows no indication when the active data source fetch fails
description:
Steve's report (2026-08-18): switched from Direct to Service with the service disabled, and the menu bar number just sat there unchanged -- no indication anything was wrong. Root cause: MenuBarStatusLabel only reacts to reading/freshness, never to AQIRefreshController.lastError. The cached reading was still within its freshness TTL (fetched moments earlier under Direct mode), so it kept rendering as if everything were fine even though the just-attempted Service-mode fetch had failed. The popover's own stale-warning banner does surface lastError.userMessage, but that requires opening the popover -- the glance-only menu bar surface had zero error signal.

Steve picked the fix: reuse the existing stale-icon+dash fallback (same one bluegull-aqi-e70.31 already uses for a genuinely-expired reading) whenever lastError is non-nil, even if freshness is still .fresh -- not a new warning badge, matching his own stated philosophy on this view ('I never want to show stale data on the menu bar... no one will notice it's stale').
acceptance_criteria: MenuBarStatusLabel gains a lastError: AQIFetchError? param. The primary pill/number branch now also requires lastError == nil; a fresh reading with a non-nil lastError falls through to the existing icon+dash branch. BluegullAQIApp passes refreshController?.lastError through.
close_reason: MenuBarStatusLabel now falls back to the existing icon+dash treatment whenever lastError is non-nil, matching the genuinely-stale-reading path exactly. Wired through from AQIRefreshController.lastError. Tests updated, all green.

title: Refetch immediately when switching data source mode
description: Steve's question (2026-08-18): does switching Service<->Direct refetch current/pinned locations from the newly selected source? Investigated -- no. DataSourceModeToggle wrote to @AppStorage with zero side effects, unlike MenuBarLocationPicker's own onChange (bluegull-aqi-e70.21), which explicitly triggers an immediate refreshNow(). The mode change only took effect whenever something else happened to trigger the next fetch: the scheduled loop (up to ~an hour away), a location change, or (for a widget) its next cache miss. This is the same class of confusion as bluegull-aqi-dc2.1's origin story (Steve: 'changed the setting from Direct to Service, the app did not display new values... changed back to direct, all was well') -- dc2.1 only made a *failed* fetch's staleness visible via an error banner, it never added an immediate refetch on mode switch.
acceptance_criteria: DataSourceModeToggle gains an onChange callback (same pattern as MenuBarLocationPicker), wired through SettingsView to BluegullAQIApp, which triggers refreshController.refreshNow() immediately on mode change -- matching the location-picker's existing behavior exactly.
close_reason: DataSourceModeToggle now has an onChange callback wired all the way through SettingsView to AQIRefreshController.refreshNow(), matching MenuBarLocationPicker's own pattern exactly. Build + tests green.

title: Show resolved place name alongside 'Current Location' on the desktop widget face
description:
Follow-up to bluegull-aqi-e70.27 (menu bar popover + widget detail view only) -- Steve asked for the same reverse-geocoded place name on the actual desktop widget face (all 3 sizes), and specified he wants BOTH 'Current Location' AND the resolved place visible together, not one replacing the other, since there's room on all three sizes.

Also fixes a real bug in the first attempt at this: BluegullAQIWidgetTimelineProvider.timeline(for:in:) checked 'configuration.location == nil' to detect Current Location, but that only catches a not-yet-configured widget instance -- an EXPLICITLY configured Current Location widget has a real non-nil LocationOptionEntity whose own .location property is nil (see entry(for:)'s own configuredLocation derivation, which already unwraps both levels correctly). The wrong check meant the reverse-geocode branch never fired for any already-configured Current Location widget, only a brand-new one -- confirmed by Steve: 'I do not see the location caption switch.'
acceptance_criteria: BluegullAQIWidgetEntry gains a resolvedPlaceName field (separate from locationName, not a replacement). All three widget layouts (Small/Medium/Large) render it as an extra caption line below locationName when present. The timeline provider's Current-Location check uses configuration.location?.location == nil, matching entry(for:)'s own pattern.
notes:
Implementation:
- BluegullAQIWidgetEntry: new resolvedPlaceName: String? field (both inits default nil), new withResolvedPlaceName(_:) builder replacing the earlier withLocationName(_:) (removed -- unused now, wrong design anyway).
- BluegullAQIWidgetTimelineProvider.timeline(for:in:): fixed the Current Location check from 'configuration.location == nil' to 'configuration.location?.location == nil', matching entry(for:)'s own configuredLocation derivation a few lines above. This was the actual bug Steve hit live -- the old check only matched a not-yet-configured widget instance, never an already-configured Current Location one.
- SmallWidgetLayout/MediumWidgetLayout/LargeWidgetLayout: each gained a resolvedPlaceName: String? param, rendered as an extra caption line directly below the existing locationName line (same font/style), only when non-nil. All three sizes, per Steve's explicit 'plenty of space' call.

Verified: make test-swift green (updated BluegullAQIWidgetEntryTests for the rename). Also had to run 'make widget-reset' again -- a THIRD conflicting widget-extension registration (this time from a stale ArchiveIntermediates path left over from an earlier 'make app-package' run) was still hanging around across the multi-day gap, on top of the /Applications one from before. pluginkit now shows exactly one clean registration pointing at the current dev build.
close_reason: Fixed the Current-Location detection bug and changed the design to show both the generic label and the resolved place name together, per Steve's explicit preference. All three widget sizes updated, tests green.

title: Stop shipping every build as '1.0': real marketing version + build number + git SHA in Settings
description: Steve's feedback (2026-08-14): three separate DMGs have gone out to a tester (Simson) all labeled '1.0', making them indistinguishable. macOS apps have two version numbers: CFBundleShortVersionString (marketing, human-bumped) and CFBundleVersion (build number, must monotonically increase). Plan: set MARKETING_VERSION to an honest pre-1.0 value in project.yml, auto-derive CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION from 'git rev-list --count HEAD' at build time via xcodebuild command-line override (no manual bookkeeping, no pbxproj/project.yml edits per build), and stamp the git short SHA into Info.plist (GitCommitSHA key, also via command-line override + $(GIT_COMMIT_SHA) expansion) so a distributed DMG can be traced to an exact commit. Surfaced in SettingsView so a tester can read it off directly. Steve: 'don't need to coordinate them to Git at the moment except maybe to embed a commit string in the package somewhere visible.'
notes:
Implementation:
- project.yml: MARKETING_VERSION 1.0 -> 0.1.0 on both targets (container app + widget). Added GIT_COMMIT_SHA build setting (default 'unknown').
- Both targets' Info.plist properties now explicitly set CFBundleShortVersionString: $(MARKETING_VERSION) and CFBundleVersion: $(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION) as literal placeholder strings -- REQUIRED, not cosmetic: discovered xcodegen only bakes those two keys as literal values the FIRST time it creates an Info.plist, then leaves them alone on every later 'generate' since they aren't declared under properties. That's exactly how three ad-hoc builds all shipped reading a stale hardcoded '1.0'/'1' even though nothing was wrong with the settings themselves. Also added GitCommitSHA: $(GIT_COMMIT_SHA).
- Makefile: new GIT_SHA (short SHA, +'-dirty' suffix if the tree has uncommitted changes) and GIT_BUILD_NUMBER (git rev-list --count HEAD) variables; XCODEBUILD_VERSION_OVERRIDES passed on the command line to both app-build and app-package's xcodebuild invocations, so the build number/commit stamp are always fresh with zero manual bookkeeping.
- New AppVersionInfo.swift (BluegullAQI target): pure displayString(shortVersion:buildNumber:gitCommitSHA:) plus a Bundle.main-backed .current, defensively drops an unexpanded '$(GIT_COMMIT_SHA)' literal (raw Xcode build bypassing the Makefile).
- SettingsView: caption at the bottom showing e.g. 'v0.1.0 (171) · d5bd66a'.

Verified end-to-end: make app-build -> built Info.plist shows 0.1.0 / 171 / d5bd66a-dirty (dirty correctly flagged, tree had uncommitted changes at build time). codesign --verify passes on the app and widget. make test-swift green (added AppVersionInfoTests).
close_reason: Marketing version reset to 0.1.0, build number auto-derived from git commit count, git SHA stamped into Info.plist and shown in Settings. Verified the Info.plist actually reflects it after a real build -- the xcodegen stale-literal gotcha would have silently defeated this otherwise.

title: Pinned Locations list should scroll past 10 entries instead of growing the window
description: Steve's feedback (2026-08-14), running the real app: PinnedLocationsView.swift renders its ForEach(locations) list directly in SettingsView's VStack with no ScrollView/List and no cap, so a long list of pins just keeps growing the Settings window vertically (SettingsView uses .windowResizability(.contentSize), which derives the window's size from content). Wants the list to comfortably fit up to 10 pinned locations at its natural size, and become internally scrollable once there are more than that, rather than the window itself growing unbounded.
acceptance_criteria: With <=10 pinned locations, the list renders at its natural height like today. With >10, the list area scrolls internally (e.g. wrapped in a ScrollView with a max height sized for ~10 rows) instead of the Settings window continuing to grow.

title: Pinned Locations descriptive text truncates instead of wrapping in Settings
description: Steve's feedback (2026-08-14), running the real app: the explanatory caption above the pinned-locations list in PinnedLocationsView.swift:39 ('Each desktop widget can be set to show one of these locations...') truncates instead of wrapping onto multiple lines in the Settings window. It's a plain Text with no explicit line-limit or fixedSize, so the truncation is coming from some layout constraint in its container (SettingsView's HStack/VStack context, or the window's own contentSize-driven sizing) rather than an intentional modifier -- needs investigation, not just adding .fixedSize blindly.
acceptance_criteria: The caption text wraps to as many lines as needed and is fully readable in the Settings window, at both the window's minimum and ideal width (SettingsView: minWidth 420, idealWidth 460).
close_reason: Fixed as part of bluegull-aqi-a22: .fixedSize(horizontal:false,vertical:true) applied to the Pinned Locations caption.

title: Manual verification: dev service URL override against a real alternate AWS server
description: bluegull-aqi-e70.28 added a hidden Settings field (Option-click the 'Settings' title) that redirects BluegullServiceClient's requests to an override URL, App Group-backed so the widget extension sees it too. Unit tests (BluegullServiceClientTests) confirm the client picks up and uses the override against a mocked request -- but nothing has verified it end-to-end against a real, different, deployed server (e.g. a second AWS stack/stage). Steve: 'don't want to do it now' (2026-08-14) -- do this before the App Store release, not urgently.
acceptance_criteria: Point the hidden override field at a real alternate AWS-deployed backend URL (different from the dev.aqi.bluegull.solutions stack) and confirm a live fetch through the menu bar actually hits that server and returns real data, not the default backend.

title: Verification plan for the helper (mostly not unit-testable)
description:
Most of this epic is OS-integration behaviour that unit tests can't reach -- launchd lifecycle, TCC grants, XPC Activity scheduling, background-item revocation. Needs a written manual verification script in the same spirit as bluegull-aqi-e70.8 and mtm.9.

At minimum: clean install first-run prompt count; helper refreshes with the app quit; helper exits when idle rather than lingering; toggling the background item off is detected and surfaced; reboot with no login (agent must NOT be login-scoped -- no RunAtLoad); widget shows fresh data after hours with the app never launched. The os_log instrumentation pattern from the spike (subsystem + category, streamed with log stream) worked well and should be kept in the shipping helper at .debug level.
acceptance_criteria: A documented manual verification checklist exists and has been run end to end on a real Mac at least once.

title: Migration for existing installs
description:
Users upgrading from a build where the app owned location.

SIMPLIFIED 2026-09-01 by Steve's decision on hib.1 (Option 1: helper only, no app-side fallback). The open question this issue used to carry -- "consider whether the app's own location grant should be relinquished or kept as the degraded-mode fallback" -- is now answered: NEITHER. It is not kept as a fallback, because there is no fallback. And it is not relinquished, because we cannot: locationd grants are not removable by us (tccutil has no authority over them and fails -10814, see hib.2). The app's existing grant simply becomes unused once the app stops calling CLLocationManager.

That makes the migration close to trivial, which is worth stating plainly so this does not get over-engineered:

ON FIRST LAUNCH OF THE HELPER-ENABLED VERSION
- Register the agent (hib.3).
- The app stops requesting location authorization and stops resolving GPS (hib.6). Its old grant goes quiet; nothing needs to be revoked.
- The helper asks for its own grant -- ONE new prompt, at the moment described in hib.6's first-run design, not whenever the system happens to wake it.
- Pinned locations are unaffected end to end. They never needed a location grant.

WHAT COULD STILL STRAND SOMEONE, and is the actual work here: the window between upgrading and the helper's first successful write. Until the helper has run once and been granted, the current-location cache entry is whatever the old app last wrote. That entry ages normally and eventually goes stale under the existing TTLs, which is correct behaviour -- but if the user declines the helper's prompt, or never sees it, they land in hib.7's state with no obvious connection to the upgrade they just did. The upgrade path should make that connection explicit rather than leaving them to infer it.

Also worth checking on a real upgrade rather than assuming: whether an existing Current Location widget keeps rendering from the pre-upgrade cache entry during that window, or blanks. It should keep rendering, aged and labelled, per dc2.5's stale-while-revalidate design.
acceptance_criteria: An upgrade from the previous shipping build ends with a working Current Location widget and NO MORE THAN ONE new permission prompt (the helper's). Pinned locations never break at any point in the upgrade. If the user declines the helper's prompt, the app explains the consequence in terms of the upgrade they just performed rather than dropping them into a generic error.

title: Detect and explain when the helper is disabled, unapproved, or absent
description:
Once the helper is the sole location owner (hib.6), its absence must be handled. Cases: the user switches the background item off in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions (silent, at any time); SMAppService.status == .requiresApproval; registration failed; the helper crashed or was never installed.

RESCOPED 2026-09-01 by Steve's decision on hib.1 (Option 1 of three). This is NO LONGER a fallback task. The app does not resolve location itself when the helper is off. This issue is now: DETECT the condition, EXPLAIN it honestly, and OFFER a way back. That removes the contradiction this issue previously had with hib.6, which required exactly one prompt and no app-side fetch while this one required an app-side location grant to fall back on.

WHY NO FALLBACK (recorded here so it is not re-litigated): an app-side fallback only works while the app is open, but the widget refreshes whether the app is open or not. The result would be the popover showing fresh AQI and the widget showing stale AQI for the same "Current Location" -- one feature, two numbers, and nothing telling the user why. Failing cleanly on both surfaces is consistent with dc2.7 and e70.31, where an honest "this is old" was chosen over a number quietly pretending to be current.

WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE:
- Both surfaces agree. Menu bar, popover and widget all reflect the same state; none of them invents a fresher number than the others.
- The app says what happened in plain language -- background refresh is off because the login item was disabled -- not a generic error.
- There is a button. Re-registering, or deep-linking to Login Items & Extensions, so the user is not left to find it.
- Pinned locations are visibly unaffected, so the product degrades by one feature rather than appearing broken.
- Must interact correctly with e70.31: a stale reading still must not appear in the menu bar.

DETECTION IS THE HARD PART, and it is why this issue carries real work rather than just copy. There is no notification when a user disables a background item; hib.3 already flags this as the nasty part -- failure is invisible and deferred, which is strictly worse than a denied prompt that fails loudly at a moment the user understands. Polling SMAppService.status is the available mechanism (the same polling mitigation LaunchAtLoginToggle already uses for the main app, with the same caveat that it is a mitigation and not a guarantee). Worth also treating a long gap since the last successful helper write as corroborating evidence, since the cache already records fetch timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: With the background item switched off: the app and the widget show the SAME honest state (no surface shows a fresher number than another), the app explains in plain language that background refresh is disabled and why, and offers a working path to re-enable. Pinned locations keep working throughout. No silent failure, and no stale reading in the menu bar (e70.31).
notes: See the contradiction note appended to bluegull-aqi-hib.6 on 2026-08-30: this issue's app-side location fallback cannot coexist with hib.6's 'exactly one prompt / no app-side fetch' acceptance criteria as both are currently written.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
.notAuthorized is now a real, distinguishable signal (2026-09-01). HelperRefreshJob.Outcome separates 'no grant' from 'authorized but no fix' from 'fetch failed' -- so 'the helper is disabled or unapproved' does not arrive at this issue disguised as a generic failure. LocationHelperController.status exposes SMAppService.Status, and refreshNow() returns nil when the helper cannot be reached at all, which is the third distinct case.

Nothing surfaces any of it in UI yet. That is still entirely this issue.

title: Make the helper the SOLE location owner (one grant, one fetcher)
description:
The helper is a separate bundle and therefore a separate TCC identity, so it needs its OWN location grant. Apple sidesteps this with the private com.apple.locationd.effective_bundle, which third parties cannot use. Done naively that means the user sees TWO location prompts, app and helper, which is a bad first run.

Fix by inverting ownership: the helper becomes the only process that resolves GPS and fetches for the current-location case. The menu bar app and the widget both just READ the App Group cache, exactly as the widget already does. One grant, one fetcher, no duplicated AirNow calls.

DECIDED 2026-09-01 (Steve, on hib.1): the app does NOT keep a location grant as a fallback. Option 1 of the three laid out on hib.1 -- helper only. See the sibling issue hib.7, which is now a DETECT-AND-EXPLAIN task rather than a fallback task; the two no longer contradict each other.

WHY NOT KEEP AN APP-SIDE FALLBACK: it half-fixes the problem, and the half it fixes is the half that makes the product inconsistent. An app-side fallback only works while the app is open; the widget refreshes whether the app is open or not. So with the background item switched off, the popover would show fresh AQI and the widget would show stale AQI -- same feature, two different numbers, and no signal to the user that anything is wrong. Failing cleanly on both surfaces is the same call already made in dc2.7 and e70.31: an honest "this is old" beats a number quietly pretending to be current.

CONCRETE APP-SIDE CHANGES THIS IMPLIES:
- BluegullAQIApp.swift:41 constructs LocationPermissionRequester(requestOnInit: !isRunningTests), which triggers the system location dialog on launch. That must go: under this design the app never resolves GPS, so it must never ask. Getting this wrong is the single easiest way to ship two prompts by accident.
- The app's current-location fetch paths (AQIRefreshController.swift:176 and :265) stop calling locationResolver.currentLocation() and read the cache instead.
- CLGeocoder is unaffected -- pinned-location address lookup and reverse geocoding need network access, not location authorization (see LocationResolver's own doc comment). Pinned locations keep working with no grant at all.

FIRST-RUN DESIGN, from what hib.10 question 5 actually measured (2026-09-01). The mechanism works -- a headless launchd-started helper got a prompt in 0.2s, a grant at 5.4s and a fix at 35m accuracy -- but three things around it are not yet designed and belong here:
1. TIMING. In the spike the prompt fired on the SYSTEM's schedule, ~70s after registration, with a human primed to watch for it. In production that could be hours after install, mid-task, from a process the user does not recognise, with no context for the ask. The app should deliberately start the helper's first run at the moment the user turns on Current Location, so the prompt arrives with a reason attached.
2. NAME. The prompt quotes the HELPER's CFBundleDisplayName. The spike's said "BlueGull AQI Location Probe". The shipping helper needs a name the user reads as BlueGull AQI.
3. TRANSACTION. The probe held no xpc transaction while waiting to be answered, so launchd considered it idle and reapable; it survived only because the answer came in 5.4 seconds. A real user may take a minute. The first-run path must hold a transaction across an unbounded human decision -- which is in direct tension with pressured exit everywhere else, so it needs to be deliberate rather than incidental.
design:
FIRST-RUN DESIGN (drafted 2026-09-01, after Steve's Option 1 decision on hib.1).

WHY AT INSTALL/UPDATE TIME. Steve's instinct, and the code supports it rather than merely permitting it: .currentLocation is the DEFAULT. MenuBarLocationPicker starts at [.currentLocation], a missing or dangling selection resolves to it, and WidgetLocationOptions.all always lists it first. So a fresh install is already using Current Location from the first second -- install time and point-of-use are the same moment. The usual objection to front-loading a permission ("don't ask before the user has expressed interest") does not apply, because the default expresses it for them. This also preserves today's timing: the app already asks at launch via LocationPermissionRequester(requestOnInit:).

THE ASYMMETRY THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING ELSE. The system location prompt is ONE SHOT and unrecoverable by us: CoreLocation refuses to re-prompt once answered, and the locationd record cannot be cleared (tccutil -10814, hib.2). Under Option 1 there is no app-side fallback, so a "Don't Allow" kills Current Location outright. That makes the cost of asking at a badly-understood moment much higher than the cost of asking slightly later.

THE KEY MOVE: gate the one-shot system prompt behind an in-app explanation we control. Ours is re-askable; the system's is not. A user who says "Not now" to ours has cost us nothing.

SEQUENCE
1. First launch after install (or after the update that introduces the helper), the app OPENS ITS POPOVER automatically, once. This is the closest moment to install at which the user is actually looking at BlueGull. A menu bar app has no main window, so there is no natural place for a launch sheet, and a bare menu bar icon showing "unavailable" is too passive -- it reads as broken rather than as needing setup.
2. The popover shows a short explanation and two choices: enable background updates, or not now. Plain language about what it does, not about helpers or agents.
3. On enable: the app registers the agent (hib.3), then pokes it to run IMMEDIATELY (see the mach-service note below) so the prompt lands while the user is still looking at the thing that just asked.
4. The helper starts, OPENS AN XPC TRANSACTION, and calls requestWhenInUseAuthorization. The system prompt appears, attributed to the helper's CFBundleDisplayName -- which must therefore read as BlueGull AQI, not as a separate-sounding product.
5. The user answers. The helper records the outcome, does its first fetch if granted, ends its transaction and exits.
6. The app reflects the result. It should show a determinate "waiting for permission" state between steps 3 and 5, with a timeout, rather than a spinner that can hang forever.

BRANCHES
- "Not now": no system prompt was consumed. Current Location shows as needing setup, with a working "Turn on" affordance. Re-askable indefinitely. This is the branch the whole pre-prompt exists to make possible.
- "Don't Allow" at the system prompt: now unrecoverable by us. The app must say so honestly and point at System Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services, which is the only remaining path. This is hib.7's copy, reached by a different route.
- Upgrade rather than fresh install: existing users already granted the APP location, and the app is about to stop using it. The explanation should acknowledge the upgrade ("BlueGull now keeps this up to date in the background") so a fresh permission request does not read as an arbitrary new demand for something they already granted once. See hib.8.
- User adds a Current Location widget without ever opening the app: the widget shows an honest needs-setup state directing them to open BlueGull. The app cannot be driven from the widget gallery, and a prompt from a process the user did not just interact with is exactly what this design exists to avoid.

ENABLING WORK NOT CURRENTLY IN ANY ISSUE: the app needs a way to start the helper ON DEMAND. Registration alone does not start it -- hib.10 measured runs=0 and state="not running" immediately after a successful register(), which is correct for a job with no RunAtLoad. Waiting for the activity to fire naturally is precisely the uncontrolled timing this design rejects. That means a MachServices entry in the helper's plist and an XPC connection from the app, which the spike deliberately skipped.

SANDBOX CONSTRAINT ON THAT, UNVERIFIED AND WORTH CHECKING EARLY: a sandboxed app cannot look up an arbitrary mach service. The sanctioned route for App Store builds is a service name prefixed with the app group identifier (group.solutions.bluegull.aqi...); com.apple.security.temporary-exception.mach-lookup.global-name is the alternative and is a poor thing to carry into App Review. Verify the app-group-prefixed name works between two sandboxed processes before building the flow on top of it.

ALSO UNVERIFIED: whether the helper's prompt reliably comes to the front when the app is frontmost. In the hib.10 probe CoreLocationAgent drew the prompt with no app frontmost at all, so it is likely fine, but the whole design assumes the user sees it immediately.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly ONE location permission prompt across a clean install and first run, and it comes from the helper, at a moment the user has just asked for Current Location. No AQI fetch and no CLLocationManager authorization request originates from the app or the widget for the current-location case. Pinned locations work with no location grant present at all.
notes: CONTRADICTION WITH hib.7, flagged 2026-08-30 during the hib.1 design review. This issue's acceptance criteria are "exactly one location permission prompt across a clean install and first run" and "no AQI fetch originates from the app or the widget for the current-location case." hib.7's fallback behaviour requires the app to resolve location itself when the helper is disabled -- which requires the app to hold its OWN location grant, i.e. a second prompt (violating criterion 1) and an app-side fetch (violating criterion 2). Deferring the app's prompt until the moment the helper is found broken satisfies criterion 1 on a clean install but asks for a permission at the worst possible moment. Pick one deliberately before building either.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
ENABLING WORK IS NOW IN PLACE (2026-09-01). This issue's 'ENABLING WORK NOT CURRENTLY IN ANY ISSUE' paragraph -- the app needs a way to start the helper on demand -- is built: LocationHelperController.refreshNow() connects to LocationHelperIdentity.machServiceName (app-group-prefixed, so no new entitlement and no growth in fw4.8's review surface) and the helper listens on it and runs a refresh. The sandbox constraint this issue flagged as 'UNVERIFIED AND WORTH CHECKING EARLY' was checked -- hib.11, with a negative control.

Also in place: item 2, NAME. The helper's CFBundleDisplayName is 'BlueGull AQI', not the spike's 'BlueGull AQI Location Probe'. That is the string the location prompt quotes and the name that appears in Login Items & Extensions.

STILL THIS ISSUE'S: item 1 (timing -- the pre-prompt in the popover, and calling register() at all), item 3 (holding a transaction across an unbounded human decision), the removal of BluegullAQIApp.swift's LocationPermissionRequester, and moving AQIRefreshController's two current-location paths onto the cache.

The helper deliberately does NOT request authorization today. Settling a status and asking for one are different acts; only the first is hib.4's. With no grant HelperRefreshJob returns .notAuthorized.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
DONE 2026-09-01, branch feat/location-helper-agent.

ONE DESIGN CHANGE, forced. This issue's step 1 -- 'the app OPENS ITS POPOVER automatically, once' -- is not buildable. MenuBarExtra has exactly two initializers (content:label: and isInserted:content:label:) and no API to present its window programmatically; checked against the SDK, not assumed. And it would not work if it existed: a .window-style MenuBarExtra popover is a lightweight NSPanel that dismisses itself when it loses key status, and the system location prompt IS a focus change -- so the explanation would vanish underneath the dialog it triggered, taking step 6's 'determinate waiting-for-permission state' with it. Built as a real Window(id: 'location-setup') instead, opened programmatically from the always-rendered MenuBarExtra label's .task. This app already opens two Window scenes that way, for a closely related reason: AQIPopoverView already documents why Settings is a window rather than a sheet over the popover.

WHAT SHIPPED. LocationSetupView + LocationSetupCoordinator implement the sequence: our re-askable explanation, then (only on yes) register the agent, poke it, and a determinate waiting state with a deadline. Five phases: explaining / registering+waiting / granted / refused / unanswered / failed. Refused and unanswered are deliberately distinct -- refused is permanent and points at System Settings; unanswered spent nothing and can be retried. 'Not now' persists so the window stops volunteering at launch, but the popover keeps offering indefinitely, which is the whole point of a pre-prompt that is free to decline.

Item 2 (NAME) was already done in hib.2 -- helper CFBundleDisplayName is 'BlueGull AQI'.
Item 3 (TRANSACTION) is LocationAuthorizationRequester, in the HELPER target, not the package: the package is linked into the app and the widget too, and a prompting call in shared code is the easiest way to reintroduce the second prompt. It holds the launchd transaction across a 120s bounded human decision.

NEW PIECE THIS NEEDED: LocationHelperStatusStore. The app cannot discover the helper's grant any other way -- a grant belongs to a bundle id, no API lets one process read another bundle's TCC state, and under Option 1 the app has no grant of its own to consult. The helper writes its authorization on EVERY run, so a revocation in System Settings surfaces on the next wake rather than never. hib.7 will read this.

OWNERSHIP INVERSION, all three call sites:
- BluegullAQIApp.swift's LocationPermissionRequester is GONE, and so is the type.
- AQIRefreshController no longer takes a LocationResolver at all -- removed the dependency rather than leaving it unused, so 'the app never asks CoreLocation for a fix' is structural.
- e70.10's 'keep the current-location slot warm while pinned' block is deleted; the helper owns that slot outright now and refreshes it regardless of what the menu bar shows, which is the same guarantee by a better route.
- fetchIfNeeded(for: nil) reads the helper's slot instead of resolving GPS.

STRUCTURAL, not just by inspection: com.apple.security.personal-information.location and NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription are removed from the APP. With them present, any future call site could quietly reintroduce the second prompt and nothing would fail.

SingleLocationPromptTests encodes the acceptance criteria as a test: no prompting call in the app, the widget, or the shared package; no location entitlement on app or widget; the helper has both the entitlement and the usage string; the helper's display name reads as BlueGull AQI. VERIFIED TO BITE -- temporarily adding requestWhenInUseAuthorization to an app file fails it with a named file and reason.

273 package tests + 39 app tests pass.

ONE LIVE CHECK OWED, and it is on this issue's own acceptance criteria: 'Pinned locations work with no location grant present at all.' That rests on CLGeocoder needing only network access, not location authorization -- documented in LocationResolver and consistent with Apple's docs, but never exercised on a signed sandboxed build WITHOUT the location entitlement, because we always had it before. If it turns out CLGeocoder needs it, pinned-address lookup and ResolvedPlaceNameCaption break and the entitlement has to come back. Check this first on the first signed build.

title: Schedule wakeups with XPC Activity rather than a timer
description:
Use xpc_activity_register for periodic refresh, mirroring com.apple.weatherd.notifications: GracePeriod ~900s, AllowBattery, RequireNetworkConnectivity, Priority Utility. The system then picks a moment when running is cheap, instead of us holding a wall-clock timer and waking the machine on our own schedule.

This is also the direct answer to Steve's standing concern about wasting AirNow queries refreshing data nobody is looking at: a grace period lets the OS coalesce our work with other activity, and the existing backend already bounds upstream load anyway (grid-snapped to ~1.1km via cache.LOCATION_KEY_PRECISION=2, hour-aligned TTLs, 400 cache-miss budget/hour), so AirNow load scales with populated grid cells rather than user count.
acceptance_criteria: Helper refreshes on a system-scheduled cadence with no timer of its own, and does not keep the machine awake. Cadence sanity-checked against AirNow's roughly-hourly NowCast publish rate.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-30 (hib.1 design review, verified against /System/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.weatherd.plist on this Mac). com.apple.weatherd.notifications is Repeating=FALSE. Its parameters are being copied here onto a job that must repeat. It also carries DuetRelatedApplications and RequiresBuddyComplete, private Duet scheduling hooks unavailable to us. And weatherd does not stay fresh by scheduled activity at all -- it is push-driven (MachServices com.apple.aps.weather, LaunchEvents com.apple.nsurlsessiond-events). BlueGull has no push channel, so we must poll, which is a materially different scheduling problem from the one weatherd solves. See also bluegull-aqi-hib.10: whether a repeating XPC activity even fires for an SMAppService-registered agent from cold boot is untested, and this issue's whole approach depends on it.
Effort note (2026-08-31): most of this issue already exists as working code in spike/hib10/ -- the LaunchEvents -> com.apple.xpc.activity plist block is written, registered, and measured over 247 wakes and a reboot. What remains here is porting it to the real helper and choosing the production Interval/Delay. See hib.1's correction comment for why the epic's 'costs weeks' figure was retracted.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 (spike/hib10, branch feat/location-helper-agent). Two corrections and one confirmation for this issue's design.

CONFIRMED: system-scheduled repeating wakeups work exactly as this issue hopes, and better than expected -- via LaunchEvents -> com.apple.xpc.activity DECLARED IN THE PLIST, not xpc_activity_register in code. Five for five over 23 minutes against a 300s Interval, with the container app quit and the agent having never previously run. Use the plist form: it has no bootstrap hole, because launchd knows the schedule at registration time rather than needing our code to have run first. Pick it up in the agent with xpc_activity_register(name, XPC_ACTIVITY_CHECK_IN, handler).

CORRECTION 1 -- RequireNetworkConnectivity is not a public constant. It does not appear in xpc/activity.h at all. weatherd sets it in its plist and this issue proposes copying it, but it cannot be set from code against a documented key and it is not contract. The public criteria are: Interval, Repeating, Delay, GracePeriod, Priority (Maintenance|Utility), AllowBattery, RequireScreenSleep, PreventsDeviceSleep, RequireHDDSpinning. Public interval constants: 1/5/15/30 min, 1/4/8 hours, 1/7 days -- an hourly cadence is first-class.

CORRECTION 2 -- "no timer of its own, and does not keep the machine awake" is satisfied, but "helper refreshes on a system-scheduled cadence" needs a caveat this issue's acceptance criteria should state: an Interval with no explicit Delay implies a Delay of HALF the interval (documented in xpc/activity.h). Measured: first fire at 152s against a 300s interval. So an hourly helper populates the cache ~30 minutes after install, not ~60. If a fresher first run matters, set Delay explicitly.

ALSO MEASURED, relevant to this issue's premise: the agent does NOT exit between wakes despite EnablePressuredExit + EnableTransactions + correct xpc_transaction_begin/end bracketing. One pid served all five wakes over 23 minutes. Pressured exit makes a process eligible for termination under memory pressure; it does not reap an idle job. Footprint while resident: 2.9 MB phys_footprint, 0.0% CPU. See hib.10 for the full data and what it does to the Option 2 vs Option 3 comparison.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
PORTED 2026-09-01 into mac-app/BluegullAQI/LaunchAgents/solutions.bluegull.aqi.locationhelper.plist. LaunchEvents -> com.apple.xpc.activity, picked up with XPC_ACTIVITY_CHECK_IN. No RunAtLoad, no KeepAlive. RequireNetworkConnectivity deliberately absent (not a public constant).

PRODUCTION CADENCE CHOSEN -- Steve, this is the one number here worth a second opinion. Interval 1800, Delay 300, GracePeriod 900.

Interval 1800 against a 3600s soft TTL is NOT 2x the fetches. GracePeriod lets the system defer a wake, so at Interval 3600 a deferred wake can leave the current-location slot soft-stale for the rest of a whole cycle. Waking twice per TTL removes that window; HelperRefreshJob then returns .skippedStillFresh without resolving GPS or fetching when the slot is still fresh, so the FETCH cadence stays ~hourly, matching AirNow's NowCast publish rate. The wake is the cheap part; the fetch is the part worth rationing. LocationHelperIdentityTests asserts Interval stays below the soft TTL so the pair can't be split by accident later.

Delay is explicit because an Interval with no Delay implies half the interval -- without it a fresh install waits ~15 min for its first background refresh. hib.6's flow pokes the mach service immediately anyway; this is the backstop for every path that doesn't.

title: Helper resolves location, fetches, and writes the App Group cache
description:
The actual job. On wake: resolve GPS, fetch AQI via the current DataSourceMode, write the reading into the shared App Group cache (including the aqi-cache-current-location slot), then end its transaction so launchd can reap it.

Reuse BluegullAQIKit wholesale -- AQIFetchCoordinator, AppGroupCache, DataSourceModeStore, LocationResolver all already work in a non-app process (the spike proved a plain helper gets CoreLocation fine).

FIX A LATENT BUG WHILE HERE: SystemLocationProvider.currentLocation() (LocationResolver.swift:82) reads manager.authorizationStatus synchronously microseconds after constructing CLLocationManager and throws .permissionDenied on .notDetermined. That is a real CoreLocation race -- the status isn't populated until the manager round-trips with locationd. A long-lived app never notices; a short-lived helper woken by launchd absolutely can. Wait for locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization before judging the status.
acceptance_criteria: With the menu bar app not running, a wake cycle refreshes the current-location cache entry, and a Current Location widget shows fresh data on its next timeline. Verified by quitting the app, clearing the slot, and observing the helper repopulate it.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
DONE 2026-09-01, branch feat/location-helper-agent.

HelperRefreshJob (BluegullAQIKit) is the job: skip-if-fresh, resolve GPS, fetch on the current DataSourceMode, write BOTH the coordinate-keyed entry (via AQIFetchCoordinator, which also records the global success/failure stamps) and the dedicated current-location slot. Never throws -- every failure is an Outcome value, because the caller has a launchd transaction to end either way. 8 unit tests.

Deliberately lives in the package, not in the helper executable, so it is testable at all: the helper process only ever runs because launchd started it.

THE LATENT BUG THIS ISSUE NAMED IS FIXED. SystemLocationProvider.currentLocation() read authorizationStatus synchronously microseconds after constructing CLLocationManager and threw .permissionDenied on .notDetermined. It now waits for the first locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization -- the manager calls that once as soon as it has a real answer -- with a 3s deadline as a backstop for a manager that never reports at all. Taking the FIRST callback (rather than waiting for a decided status) matters: 'no grant yet' is the normal state before hib.6, and it must fail fast rather than burn the deadline on every wake. 5 new tests, including one that a real denial still denies and one that an already-decided status pays nothing.

TWO DESIGN CHOICES WORTH REVIEW:
1. The job returns .skippedStillFresh when the current-location slot is still within its soft TTL -- no GPS fix, no fetch. This is what makes the sub-TTL wake interval free (see hib.5).
2. The helper does NOT request authorization. Settling a status and asking for one are different acts; the ask is hib.6's, because it has to hold a transaction across an unbounded human decision at a moment the user has just asked for Current Location. With no grant this reports .notAuthorized, which is the input hib.7 needs.

NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE: the acceptance criterion (quit the app, clear the slot, watch the helper repopulate it) needs a registered agent with a location grant, which needs hib.6's first-run flow or a manual grant. Structural verification done: the built bundle has the plist at Contents/Library/LaunchAgents and the executable exactly where BundleProgram names it.

title: Register/unregister the helper via SMAppService.agent, and handle revocation
description:
Container app registers the agent on first launch (the widget extension cannot -- app extensions cannot spawn processes or call SMAppService, which is why 'first widget starts the daemon' was never possible).

LaunchAgent plist modelled on com.apple.weatherd.plist: MachServices, EnablePressuredExit=true, EnableTransactions=true, ProcessType=Adaptive, and deliberately NO RunAtLoad and NO KeepAlive, so it is on-demand rather than login-scoped. This is what makes 'not started at login' achievable, which was Steve's explicit requirement.

REVOCATION IS THE NASTY PART: an SMAppService background item is enabled by default and appears in System Settings > General > Login Items & Extensions, where the user can switch it off at any time. The agent then silently stops and the app has no event for it -- failure is invisible and deferred, which is strictly worse than a denied prompt that fails loudly at a moment the user understands. Poll SMAppService.status for .requiresApproval and surface it in the popover.
acceptance_criteria: Agent registers on first launch and appears in Login Items & Extensions. Toggling it off is detected via SMAppService.status and surfaced to the user rather than failing silently. Unregisters cleanly on uninstall.
notes: Effort note (2026-08-31): spike/hib10/Container/ContainerApp.swift already implements register/unregister/status against SMAppService.agent, including the headless HIB10_ACTION path and status mapping. The revocation-detection half of this issue is still unbuilt. See hib.1's correction comment.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
HALF DONE 2026-09-01. mac-app/BluegullAQI/LocationHelperController.swift has the mechanism: register (unregister-first, per SMAppService.h's warning that a changed plist or executable needs re-registration -- every app update changes the executable, so a plain register() on an existing registration is the stale-agent bug waiting to happen), unregister (which removes the Background Task Management record; launchctl bootout alone does not), status, and refreshNow() -- the on-demand poke over the app-group-prefixed mach service, ported from hib.11.

STILL OPEN, and it is the harder half: revocation detection. Nothing yet polls SMAppService.status for .requiresApproval or surfaces it. That is this issue's real substance and it is untouched.

DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED INTO APP LAUNCH. Registering the agent makes it start prompting for location on the system's own schedule, which is exactly the uncontrolled first run hib.6 exists to prevent. This type is the mechanism; hib.6 owns when register() is called and what the user sees first. Wiring it up before hib.6 would ship the bad first run.

title: Scaffold helper agent target with a FRESH bundle id
description:
New LSUIElement, sandboxed helper target embedded in the app at Contents/Library/LaunchAgents (or Contents/MacOS for an SMAppService.agent program), signed with team G5DWPBWHQ5.

CRITICAL: do NOT reuse the bundle id 'solutions.bluegull.aqi.helper'. The 2026-08-12 spike left a real, still-present locationd grant for that identifier in /var/db/locationd/clients.plist (Authorized=true, pinned to that bundle id plus Steve's 'Apple Development: Steven Barber' leaf cert). It could not be removed -- tccutil has no authority over locationd-managed Location grants and fails with -10814 -- so a helper reusing that id would silently inherit a location grant, skip the first-run prompt, mask a real bug, and make any test of the genuine first-run experience invalid. Use something distinct, e.g. solutions.bluegull.aqi.locationhelper.

Entitlements needed (all public): com.apple.security.app-sandbox, com.apple.security.personal-information.location, com.apple.security.network.client, and the shared App Group group.solutions.bluegull.aqi. Keychain access group too if the helper does Direct-mode fetches.
acceptance_criteria: Helper builds, signs, launches, and writes a recognisable line to os_log. Bundle id is new and confirmed absent from /var/db/locationd/clients.plist before first run.
notes:
TWO CORRECTIONS 2026-08-30 (hib.1 design review, checked against SMAppService.h in the current SDK).
1. "Contents/Library/LaunchAgents (or Contents/MacOS for an SMAppService.agent program)" conflates two things. For SMAppService.agent(plistName:) the PLIST must be in Contents/Library/LaunchAgents; the executable is pointed at by the BundleProgram key as a bundle-relative path (SMAppService.h calls out BundleProgram specifically, so the app can be relocated after install).
2. Same header warns: if either the plist or the executable changes, the service must be RE-registered or it may not launch, and unregistering first is recommended when the executable changed. That applies to every dev iteration and to every shipped app update -- worth building into the registration code from the start rather than debugging a stale agent later.

Also, on the fresh-bundle-id reasoning: it is right, but it makes each clean first-run test consume a bundle id, since the resulting locationd grant is equally unremovable. And a dev-signed build's grant does not represent the shipping first run anyway -- the Developer ID leaf is a different signing identity from Apple Development. Plan repeatable first-run testing (VM or spare Mac) BEFORE starting this issue.
Effort note (2026-08-31): spike/hib10/ already contains a working version of this -- a sandboxed `tool` target with CREATE_INFOPLIST_SECTION_IN_BINARY giving it its own CFBundleIdentifier and its own code-signing identifier, embedded at Contents/MacOS and reached via BundleProgram. Reuse that project.yml shape rather than starting from scratch; note the two entitlement traps recorded there, both of which produce a green build and a silently unsandboxed helper.

comments.author: Steve Barber
comments.text:
DONE 2026-09-01. Target BluegullAQIHelper in mac-app/project.yml, bundle id solutions.bluegull.aqi.locationhelper -- confirmed distinct from the burnt solutions.bluegull.aqi.helper, and LocationHelperIdentityTests asserts it stays that way.

An 'application' target, not a 'tool'. The spike proved the bare tool shape for activity wakes and mach services but NEVER for CoreLocation; it proved the LSUIElement .app shape for a headless launchd-started location prompt. This reuses the shape whose risky half was the half actually measured. Nested at Contents/Library/LoginItems, codeSignOnCopy so it keeps its own signing identity -- a separate identity is the whole reason it can hold a grant the app cannot lend it.

Entitlements spelled out under properties: in project.yml, per the spike's trap (a hand-written file referenced with only path: gets replaced by an empty <dict/> on the next generate -- green build, silently unsandboxed helper). Confirmed generated correctly: app-sandbox, personal-information.location, network.client, the app group, and the keychain access group.

ACCEPTANCE, partially: it builds and the layout is verified (plist at Contents/Library/LaunchAgents, executable exactly where BundleProgram names it, no stray copy in Resources). It has NOT been signed, launched, or confirmed absent from /var/db/locationd/clients.plist before a first run -- Automatic signing will want this new bundle id registered on the developer portal, which is Steve's call to make.
