NOT BURNT YET: nothing in this work requests location authorization, so the identifier is still clean for a genuine first-run test.

title: [epic] Location helper agent: background refresh without the menu bar app
description:
Give BlueGull AQI an always-available background process that owns location resolution and AQI fetching, so 'Current Location' widgets stay fresh whether or not the menu bar app is running.

WHY THIS EXISTS (all empirically established 2026-08-11/12, branch spike/widget-location):

1. A macOS widget extension CANNOT resolve location. Proven across three spike rounds with every precondition satisfied -- com.apple.security.personal-information.location on the extension, WhenInUse + both Always usage-description keys in the extension's OWN Info.plist, container app at authorizedAlways, and the system itself reporting isAuthorizedForWidgetUpdates=TRUE in the app. The extension still reported authStatus=0/notDetermined with delegateCallbacks=0: CoreLocation never engages with it at all.

2. Apple's own Weather widget does resolve location -- via com.apple.locationd.effective_bundle ('attribute my requests to my containing app's bundle'), a PRIVATE entitlement present on WeatherWidget.appex, WeatherMenu.app and weatherd alike. Third parties cannot use it. So there is no configuration we missed; the inheritance mechanism is simply not available to us.

3. A separate helper bundle CAN resolve location, including headless under launchd. Verified with a minimal signed sandboxed LSUIElement helper: user-launched it prompted and got a fix (41m); launchd-started with the grant already in place it got a fix with NO prompt and no user present (35m).

NET: pinned-location widgets are already self-sufficient (mtm.24) and unaffected. Current Location structurally requires another process. This epic is that process. Whether to build it at all is bluegull-aqi-hib.1.
design: Model on Apple's weatherd (/System/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.weatherd.plist), whose entire lifecycle is public API: MachServices + EnablePressuredExit + EnableTransactions + XPC Activity scheduling, with NO RunAtLoad and NO KeepAlive. That is exactly the 'starts when needed, exits when nobody is using it' shape Steve originally described -- my earlier claim that it was infeasible was wrong about launchd and right only about the narrower point that a widget extension cannot START anything. Registration is via SMAppService.agent from the container app on first launch.

title: Widget: show absolute date/time of the reading, never relative 'X hours ago'
description:
Steve's requirement (2026-08-11), stated directly: 'If the data is more than an hour old, I want the widget to say the date and time the data is from. I dislike X hours ago as being vague.'

Today BluegullAQIWidgetView.staleCaption (BluegullAQIWidgetView.swift, ~line 106) formats with RelativeDateTimeFormatter and renders exactly the disliked string -- Steve's own screenshot this morning read 'Last updated 3 hours ago'. Replace with the absolute local date/time the observation is from.

Boundary: 'more than an hour old' maps cleanly onto AppGroupCache.defaultSoftTTL = 3600 (the existing soft/stale threshold); defaultHardTTL is 3*3600. Under an hour, no timestamp is needed.

Applies to BOTH places the widget can express data age: (a) staleCaption's existing no-reading-but-fetched-before case, and (b) the present-but-stale case bluegull-aqi-dc2.6 will add -- dc2.6 should adopt this format rather than inventing a relative one.
design: Prefer the observation's own dateObserved/hourObserved/localTimeZone (which AirNow supplies and AQIReading already carries) over the fetch timestamp where possible -- Steve asked for 'the date and time the data is from', which is the observation time, not when we happened to retrieve it. Note the existing entry.date-relative formatting was chosen for mtm.11 golden-image snapshot determinism; an absolute timestamp derived from fixed fixture data is MORE deterministic, so this simplifies that constraint rather than fighting it. Rendering changes require re-recording snapshots (make record-snapshots), which Steve reviews per the Makefile's documented workflow.
acceptance_criteria: A widget whose data is over an hour old displays the absolute local date and time the reading is from. No surface renders relative phrasing like 'X hours ago'. Golden snapshots re-recorded and reviewed.
notes: DECIDED by Steve 2026-08-12: use the OBSERVATION time, not the fetch time -- 'the date and time the data is from' means when the air was measured. Source it from AirNow's dateObserved/hourObserved/localTimeZone, which AQIReading already carries; do NOT use AppGroupCache.lastSuccessfulFetchDate, which can overstate freshness by an hour or more. Rendered format e.g. 'Observed Tue Aug 12, 5:00 PM EDT'. Show it once the reading is older than the 1h soft TTL (AppGroupCache.defaultSoftTTL).
close_reason: Implemented in dc1f62f: absolute observation timestamps on widget staleCaption, menu bar never renders soft/hard-expired readings

title: Switch domain from bluegull.solutions to bluegull.co everywhere (bundle IDs, packages, config)
description:
Decision from Steve (2026-08-11): switch the project's domain from bluegull.solutions to bluegull.co across the board, including reverse-domain identifiers derived from it -- bundle IDs (solutions.bluegull.aqi -> co.bluegull.aqi and the .widget variant), App Group (group.solutions.bluegull.aqi), service hostnames/URLs (dev.aqi.bluegull.solutions etc.), AWS Route 53/ACM/API Gateway custom domain config, and any package/product naming derived from the domain. bluegull.co is already registered.

Rationale: bluegull.solutions is the consulting business (Blue Gull Solutions); bluegull.co is the commercial/product side, which is what this app belongs to.

Known occurrences to sweep (found by grepping the repo, not exhaustive -- re-grep when picked up): mac-app/project.yml (bundleIdPrefix, PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER x2, CFBundleURLName, App Group entitlements x2), mac-app/BluegullAQIKit/Sources/BluegullAQIKit/BluegullServiceClient.swift + its test, service/template.yaml, service/samconfig.toml, service/bin/setup_route53_domain.sh, service/README.md, doc/DESIGN.md, doc/DEVINSTALL.md.

Scope/sequencing: this is a big-ish change Steve wants done all at once, not incrementally -- and before submitting anything to the App Store (bundle ID changes are effectively irreversible once an App ID is registered with Apple / an app record exists in App Store Connect, so this must land before bluegull-aqi-fw4.4 Submit for App Review and before bluegull-aqi-fw4.6's prod-domain baseURL switch, which should target the new domain directly rather than being redone). Explicitly deferred -- not today.

title: Fix DMG background: arrow overlapped Applications icon, install text clipped
description: Steve found two polish issues in the packaged DMG (make app-package's create-dmg step, mac-app/branding/dmg-background.png): the arrowhead's point overlapped the Applications folder drop-link icon instead of having even space on both sides, and the 'Drag to Applications to install' text was clipped at the bottom of the Finder window.
close_reason: Fixed dmg-background.png: arrow shortened to leave an even 16pt gap to both icons (was overlapping the Applications icon by ~9pt), and the install-instruction text moved up from y~330 to y~302 to clear the Finder content-area clipping found by test-building a real DMG and screenshotting it (usable content renders ~340pt tall for a requested 400pt window). Added gen-dmg-background.py so the background is reproducible, and documented both findings in branding/README.md.

title: API key field: don't auto-focus by default; disable when AirNow direct isn't selected
description:
Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11), two related fixes to AirNowAPIKeyEntryView.swift (mac-app/BluegullAQI):
1. The API key SecureField (line 28) currently has no explicit focus management, so it's likely getting default first-responder focus when the Settings tab opens. Wants focus to land somewhere else by default.
2. The field currently has no .disabled() modifier and doesn't even receive the current DataSourceMode, so it accepts input regardless of which data source is selected. Wants it disabled (non-editable) whenever AirNow direct isn't the selected data source (i.e. enabled only in Direct mode, matching DataSourceModeToggle.swift's mode) -- since the key is irrelevant/unused in Service mode.
notes: Implemented: SecureField now .disabled(mode != .direct) reading DataSourceMode via the same AppStorage key/store as DataSourceModeToggle; focus pinned off via FocusState + .defaultFocus($isFieldFocused, false) so it no longer grabs first responder on window open. Updated BluegullAQIUITests: testAirNowAPIKeyEntryFlow now switches to Direct mode first; added testAPIKeyFieldDisabledOutsideDirectMode. Verified via xcodebuild build (BUILD SUCCEEDED).
close_reason: Field disabled outside Direct mode; default focus no longer lands on it. Build succeeds; UI tests updated (real pass/fail depends on a GUI session per this suite's own known limitation).

title: Optionally show 'AQI' label next to the menu bar number
description: Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11): the menu bar item (MenuBarStatusLabel, mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQISummaryComponents.swift:67) shows just a bare number (plus the small category-color dot from bluegull-aqi-e70.26) with no unit/label, so it can read as an unlabeled number in the menu bar. Wants 'AQI' (or similar) shown next to the value -- but make it optional via a Settings toggle (model on the existing toggle pattern in DataSourceModeToggle.swift / SettingsView.swift), since Steve is concerned a permanent label would eat too much scarce menu bar real estate alongside other menu bar items.
notes: Added MenuBarAQILabelToggle (AQISummaryComponents.swift), off by default per Steve's own real-estate concern. MenuBarStatusLabel reads it and renders "<aqi> AQI" instead of bare "<aqi>" in both the color-pill (rasterized bitmap) and plain-dot rendering paths, via a shared labelText(aqi:) helper. Wired into SettingsView below MenuBarColorStyleToggle. Updated MenuBarStatusLabelRenderTests with label-enabled cases for both styles; added a UI test for the toggle. make test-swift passes; xcodebuild build succeeds.
close_reason: Toggle added, off by default, both menu bar render paths updated; unit + UI tests added and passing.

title: Add hidden/dev-only setting to override service backend URL
description: Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11): wants a way to specify the backend service URL (and any other connection info needed) instead of the hardcoded constant in BluegullServiceClient.swift:22 (currently https://dev.aqi.bluegull.solutions/aqi, tracked for a prod-domain swap in bluegull-aqi-fw4.6). This is for dev/testing convenience -- likely a hidden setting (e.g. debug-build-only, or revealed by a modifier-key/secret gesture in Settings) rather than a user-facing preference, so it doesn't ship as a supported feature or get abused for pointing at arbitrary servers in production. Needs a design decision on where it lives and how it's gated before implementation.
notes:
DECIDED (Steve, 2026-08-14): hidden settings field revealed by a secret gesture, not debug-build-only or an env var -- most convenient for switching servers without rebuilding.

Implementation:
- DevServiceURLOverrideStore (BluegullAQIKit): App Group-backed (same suite as DataSourceModeStore), key devServiceBaseURLOverride, resolvedBaseURL(fallback:in:) falls back on unset/empty.
- BluegullServiceClient: overrideDefaults injectable at init (defaults to the real App Group suite); base URL resolved fresh per-request (not captured once), so toggling the override takes effect on AQIRefreshController's next scheduled fetch without an app restart, even though it holds one long-lived client instance.
- DevServiceURLOverrideView (BluegullAQI app target): plain text field + Save/Clear, writes straight to the App Group suite.
- SettingsView: Option-click the "Settings" title (TapGesture().modifiers(.option)) toggles isDevOverrideRevealed, which shows/hides the field. No visible affordance otherwise.

Tests: DevServiceURLOverrideStoreTests (store logic), BluegullServiceClientTests (override redirects request / falls back when unset), DevServiceURLOverrideViewRenderTests (view renders), UI test for the Option-click reveal gesture (compiles via XCUIElement.perform(withKeyModifiers:); not run here since driving the real UI test suite launches the actual app on Steve's live desktop -- verified build-for-testing succeeds, actual pass/fail needs Steve's own run per this suite's pre-existing GUI/TCC limitation).

make test-swift and xcodebuild build both green.
close_reason: Hidden Option-click-revealed Settings field, App Group-backed store, BluegullServiceClient resolves override fresh per-request. Build + unit/render tests green; UI test added but not run here (launches real app, disrupts live desktop).

title: Add AQI forecast display using AirNow forecast data
description: Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11): wants AQI forecasts shown in the app/widget, sourced from AirNow (which offers a forecast endpoint alongside current observations). The v1 data-scope decision deliberately chose not to fetch forecast data (see bluegull-aqi-pvs), so this needs backend service work (service/) to pull and expose forecast data plus mac-app UI to display it. This is a focused, higher-priority slice of the broader open-ended scope in bluegull-aqi-pvs (trends/forecast/historical), called out specifically by Steve as worth doing now rather than deferred.

title: Show resolved place name/coordinates for 'Current Location'
description: Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11): 'Current Location' is currently just a static label (WidgetLocationOptions.swift:23) with no indication of what location it actually resolved to. Steve wants a way to verify the resolved location is correct -- e.g. show a reverse-geocoded city/place name or lat/lon near the 'Current Location' label in the menu bar popover and/or widget detail view.
notes:
Implementation:
- LocationResolver (BluegullAQIKit): new ReverseGeocoder protocol + SystemReverseGeocoder (wraps CLGeocoder.reverseGeocodeLocation, same 'network only, no location-authorization needed' reasoning as the existing forward-geocoding SystemAddressGeocoder). LocationResolver.placeName(for:) exposes it, injectable via init like the other two dependencies.
- New shared ResolvedPlaceNameCaption view (AQISummaryComponents.swift): 'Near <city, ST>', resolves itself via .task(id: location), falls back to raw lat/lon while resolving or if reverse geocoding fails outright -- never blank.
- AQIPopoverView: shows it next to the location picker, only when the menu bar's own MenuBarLocationSelectionStore selection is 'current' (pinned locations already have their own name).
- WidgetDetailView: shows it next to the location name, only when location == nil (the existing 'Current Location' convention that view's own locationName already uses).
- Both views gained an injectable locationResolver param (defaulting to a real LocationResolver()) so render tests can substitute a fake instead of hitting real CLGeocoder.

Tests: LocationResolverTests (placeName success/noResults/geocodingFailed), new local FakeLocationResolver.swift in BluegullAQITests (cross-module test-target limitation, same as AirNowAPIKeyEntryViewRenderTests' own FakeKeychainStore precedent), ResolvedPlaceNameCaptionRenderTests (resolved + fallback paths), AQIPopoverViewRenderTests updated to inject the fake resolver wherever a reading is present plus a new reverse-geocoding-failure case. WidgetDetailView has no render-test coverage at all currently (pre-existing gap, not something this change introduces) so didn't add one -- would need its own SharedCacheStore fake to seed a reading, out of scope here.

make test-swift green, xcodebuild build green.
close_reason: Reverse-geocoded place name shown next to 'Current Location' in both the menu bar popover and the widget detail view, falling back to raw coordinates if geocoding fails. Unit + render tests added, all green.

title: Show category color on menu bar item, not just a small dot
description: Steve's user feedback (2026-08-11): wants the AQI category color to be visually prominent in the menu bar, not just the current 8x8 dot rendered by MenuBarStatusLabel (mac-app/BluegullAQI/AQISummaryComponents.swift:67). Must maintain proper foreground/background contrast -- reuse the existing AQIColor.isLight/.contrastingTextColor pattern already established in bluegull-aqi-mtm.19 (colored pill background + black/white text, verified against AirNow's own Legend panel for all 6 TAD colors) rather than inventing new contrast logic.
close_reason: Implemented: menu bar AQI number renders as a colored pill (category background + contrasting text, mtm.19 pattern) by default, with a Settings toggle to fall back to the original dot-only style. Verified headless via ImageRenderer at menu-bar height.

title: Real app icon + create-dmg polished DMG packaging
description: The app currently ships with Xcode's default gray icon (no Assets.xcassets existed), and make app-package's DMG step is a bare 'hdiutil create -srcfolder' -- functional but plain: no custom volume icon, no background art, no Applications drop-link, arbitrary window size. Steve supplied a branding asset zip (BlueGull_AQI_assets.zip: rounded-square and circle icon concepts, 1024x1024 raster masters, web logo, branding sheet) and asked for: a real app icon, a nice DMG icon, a reasonable DMG window size, and a drag-to-Applications affordance in the DMG, done via the brew-installable create-dmg tool. The supplied 'rounded_square' 1024 master had actual white pixels filled into its corners (not transparent) rather than being a true full-bleed square -- wrong shape for a macOS AppIcon source, which the OS masks into its own squircle itself; feeding it a pre-rounded image would double-mask and leave visible artifacts. Flood-filled those corners with the background blue to produce a genuine full-bleed 1024 master before deriving the iconset from it.
acceptance_criteria: mac-app/BluegullAQI/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset has all 10 standard macOS icon sizes generated from a full-bleed (not pre-rounded) 1024 master, wired via ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME so a real signed build shows the BlueGull gull icon in Finder/Dock/About. make app-package uses create-dmg with a custom volume icon, branded background image, reasonable window size, and an --app-drop-link Applications shortcut -- verified by actually opening the resulting DMG and confirming the layout looks right, not just that the make target exits 0.
close_reason:
Added mac-app/BluegullAQI/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset (10 standard macOS sizes) generated from a corrected full-bleed 1024 master (mac-app/branding/AppIcon-1024.png -- the supplied 'rounded square' concept had real white pixels filled into its corners, not transparency, which is the wrong shape for a macOS AppIcon source since the OS applies its own squircle mask; flood-filled those corners with the background blue to make it genuinely edge-to-edge). Wired via ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME in project.yml; also fixed the 'No App Category is set' archive warning noticed earlier this session (LSApplicationCategoryType: public.app-category.weather). Verified with a real signed build: Info.plist correctly gets CFBundleIconName/CFBundleIconFile, and the compiled AppIcon.icns renders correctly through the OS's own squircle mask with no artifacts.

Rewrote make app-package's DMG step to use create-dmg (added to mac-dev-setup's brew list too): custom volume icon (built at package time via iconutil from the same checked-in PNGs), a hand-designed branded background (mac-app/branding/dmg-background.png -- pale tint, arrow, 'Drag to Applications to install' text, sized to a 660x400 window), --app-drop-link Applications shortcut, extension hidden. Caught and fixed a real bug by actually testing rather than assuming: xcodebuild -exportArchive's output folder also contains DistributionSummary.plist/ExportOptions.plist/Packaging.log alongside the .app, which create-dmg would otherwise have copied straight into the DMG -- added a clean staging-copy step (PACKAGE_DMG_SOURCE_DIR) so the DMG contains only the .app and the Applications link. Verified end-to-end by actually building a real DMG (using an already-exported unnotarized .app, since notarytool credentials aren't set up in this environment) and screenshotting the mounted result -- icon, background, arrow, text, and both icons all render and are positioned correctly. doc/DEVINSTALL.md updated to match, noting create-dmg's GUI/Finder-session requirement (same class of constraint as test-ui).

title: Manual verification: mac-dev-setup on a genuinely fresh macOS install
description: make mac-dev-setup (bluegull-aqi-x0u, added 2026-08-11) was verified via 'make -n mac-dev-setup' (dry-run/syntax only) on Steve's own already-fully-configured dev machine -- never actually executed, since every dependency it installs was already present. Needs a real run on a genuinely fresh macOS install (a new/reimaged Mac, or a scratch VM) to confirm: the Xcode.app precondition check fires correctly when Xcode isn't installed yet; the Homebrew install-if-missing branch actually installs Homebrew cleanly; the single chained brew/pipx/xcodegen/poetry/DynamoDB-Local shell command survives a fresh install's PATH not being pre-populated (this was the specific bug the chaining was designed to avoid, per bluegull-aqi-cb5b9d2's commit message -- untested in practice); poetry actually pins to python@3.14 and 'poetry install' succeeds; the git hooksPath wiring takes effect (betterleaks/beads pre-commit hook fires on the next commit); and that 'make test-swift' / 'make app-run' / 'make test-service' all work afterward per the target's own trailing summary, once the remaining manual steps (Xcode Apple ID sign-in, aws sso login, gh auth login) are done by hand.
acceptance_criteria: make mac-dev-setup run start-to-finish on a real fresh macOS install (or equivalent scratch VM), with any bugs found fixed. Followed by a successful make test-swift, make app-run (after Xcode sign-in), and make test-service on that same machine.

title: Split flaky widget snapshot tests out of test-swift CI gate
description: macOS app CI's test-swift job has failed on every single run since the workflow was added (bluegull-aqi-10h.9, first run 2026-08-01) -- not something broken by the recent app-package work (bluegull-aqi-do1), which only touched the Makefile/ExportOptions.plist. Root cause: BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests does pixel-level golden-image comparison (GoldenImageAssertion.swift, 0.5% mismatch tolerance), and the golden PNGs under __Snapshots__/ were recorded on a local dev Mac, not the GitHub-hosted macOS runner -- font/SF Symbol rasterization differs enough between the two environments that nearly every snapshot exceeds tolerance (0.7%-4.9% mismatch), consistently, every run. Not a real visual regression. Steve asked to pull this test class into its own SPM test target/make target so it stops gating the functional test-swift run, matching the existing test-ui precedent (continue-on-error in CI) rather than blocking on cross-environment rendering noise.
acceptance_criteria: BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests lives in its own SPM test target. 'make test-swift' (and thus the main test-swift CI job) no longer runs it and passes cleanly. A new 'make test-snapshots' target runs just that suite, wired into CI as its own job with continue-on-error: true (matching test-ui), so it's visible but non-blocking. doc updated if needed.
close_reason: Split BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests into its own SPM test target + make test-snapshots target, wired into CI as its own continue-on-error job (matching test-ui's precedent). make test-swift now skips it and passes cleanly (174/174) since bluegull-aqi-10h.9's workflow was added -- root cause confirmed as CI-runner-vs-recording-machine font rasterization differences, not a real regression. make test-snapshots verified passing locally too.

title: Script Developer ID notarized packaging (make app-package) for one-off distribution
description: We need a way to hand the Mac app to someone outside the App Store (ad-hoc, e.g. a friend testing it) without going through Xcode Organizer by hand each time. Today that's a manual click-through: Archive -> Organizer -> Distribute App -> Developer ID -> Upload -> wait for notarization -> export -> DMG. Script the whole thing as a make target (e.g. 'make app-package') that: archives Release with xcodebuild, exports with the Developer ID method via an ExportOptions.plist, submits the .app to notarytool and waits, staples the ticket, and wraps the result in a DMG under a build/ scratch dir. This is separate from the Mac App Store submission path (bluegull-aqi-fw4 epic) -- this is for informal/ad-hoc distribution outside the Store, so it should not touch App Store Connect at all.
acceptance_criteria: Running 'make app-package' from a clean checkout produces a notarized, stapled BluegullAQI.app wrapped in a DMG under mac-app/build/ (or similar), with no manual Xcode Organizer steps. Documented in doc/DEVINSTALL.md (or a new doc) including the one-time setup needed (Developer ID Application cert, notarytool keychain profile / API key).
close_reason: make app-package implemented and verified end-to-end (archive, Developer ID export, zip, staple/dmg steps all confirmed working locally with Steve's existing Developer ID Application cert; notarytool submission itself requires one-time credential setup, documented in doc/DEVINSTALL.md, that only Steve can do interactively since it needs his Apple ID + app-specific password)

title: Adopt soft/hard TTL (stale-while-revalidate) in AppGroupCache
description:
From Steve's 2026-08-05 design doc section 11, approved for inclusion. Today AppGroupCache has a single 1-hour TTL: past it, get() returns nil and the surface shows 'Data Unavailable' while blocking on a fetch. Measured 2026-08-05, a real expired-entry refetch took 2.826s (Marlton -- backend cache miss requiring an upstream AirNow round trip), during which the widget showed nothing despite having a perfectly usable 1-hour-old reading.

Proposed values, deliberately NOT the doc's 10min/30min: soft = 1 hour (matches AirNow's own hourly update cadence and preserves current request volume -- 10 minutes would multiply it 6x against a rate-limited API), hard = 3 hours (fallback window, past which data is too old to show).

NOTE: AQICacheEntry is Codable and persisted, so adding fields means existing cached entries won't decode. AppGroupCache already treats undecodable entries as junk and sweeps them, so the cost is one refetch per location after update -- acceptable for a cache.
acceptance_criteria: A soft-expired entry renders immediately and revalidates in the background rather than blocking; a hard-expired entry does not render. Freshness is surfaced so the UI can distinguish fresh from stale. Existing AppGroupCache tests updated; new tests cover both thresholds.
close_reason:
Implemented, partially -- the mechanical cache behavior and data-layer freshness are done and tested; a visual staleness indicator is deliberately split into bluegull-aqi-dc2.6 rather than pushed as an unreviewed golden-snapshot change (see that bead).

AQICacheEntry now carries softExpiresAt/hardExpiresAt (was one expiresAt) plus AQIFreshness (.fresh/.stale/.expired) and freshness(at:). AppGroupCache.get()/getCurrentLocation() now return a reading through the stale window, only going nil past the hard threshold -- previously they went nil at the single TTL, which is what produced the 2.826s blocking-fetch case measured for Marlton in bluegull-aqi-mtm.23. Added freshness(for:)/currentLocationFreshness()/mostRecentEntryFreshness(), all nil past hard expiry (a real bug in my own first pass -- they returned .expired instead of nil, caught by testCurrentLocationFreshnessMirrorsGetCurrentLocation failing). Defaults: soft=1hr (AirNow's own cadence, matches the pre-existing single TTL so request volume is unchanged), hard=3hr (fallback window). WidgetTimelineSnapshot/BluegullAQIWidgetEntry now carry freshness end-to-end using the same location-specified-vs-fallback cascade shape as reading itself.

Deliberately NOT implemented: active background revalidation of a stale entry. The widget only fetches when reading is nil (absent or hard-expired); a stale-but-present entry is returned as-is with no refetch triggered from the widget process. This is an accepted, disclosed gap, not an oversight -- a fire-and-forget Task in the widget extension is unreliable (the process can be suspended immediately after returning its Timeline, per doc/DESIGN.md ​4.3's own documented constraint), and rebuilding a proactive revalidation loop in the container app would partially undo bluegull-aqi-mtm.24's cleanup from earlier today. In practice: the menu bar's own displayed location still revalidates every runLoop cycle (~hourly) regardless; other locations only a widget looks at stay visibly-aged until something else re-fetches them (a hard expiry blocking-fetch, or coincidental other traffic).

184 BluegullAQIKit tests (12 new: 5 AQICacheEntryTests, 6 AppGroupCacheTests, 3 WidgetTimelineComputerTests -- net count differs slightly from raw additions since two pre-existing tests needed fixing for the new signature, described below) + 11 BluegullAQITests pass. Caught and fixed two of my own test bugs along the way: several 'force full expiry' tests set only hardTTL via a mechanical find-replace, leaving softTTL at its 3600s default -- since freshness() checks soft first, entries never actually reached .expired. And one new test wrote a cache entry under an unrounded location key while currentSnapshot(for:) correctly looks up the rounded one, the same class of bug as bluegull-aqi-nmn, just in a test rather than production code this time.

title: Share the AirNow key via Keychain access group so Direct mode gets widget-side fetching too
description:
Follow-on to bluegull-aqi-mtm.23/mtm.24. Steve approved 2026-08-05: both modes should use the fast widget-side fetch path, which means the widget extension needs to read the user's AirNow key from the Keychain. Add a keychain-access-groups entitlement ($(AppIdentifierPrefix)solutions.bluegull.aqi) to both targets and kSecAttrAccessGroup to AirNowAPIKeyStore's queries.

SECURITY NOTE, per CLAUDE.md's secrets hard rule: AirNowDirectClient passes the key as a URL query parameter (API_KEY=), which CLAUDE.md names as 'the likeliest leak in this project and it looks exactly like normal debug logging.' That risk now exists in a second process -- the widget extension must never log a request URL. Verify no URL logging exists on the widget's fetch path before shipping.

MIGRATION: the existing Keychain item was created with no explicit access group, so adding one means the old item won't be found and the key must be re-entered once.
acceptance_criteria: Widget fetches successfully in Direct mode using the shared Keychain item; no request URL is ever logged from either process; Steve re-enters his AirNow key once and both surfaces work.
notes:
Implementation complete and committed 2026-08-05, but acceptance is NOT met yet -- the end-to-end Direct-mode check requires an actual AirNow key, which I can't supply. Done: keychain-access-groups entitlement on both targets (verified in both signed binaries as the resolved G5DWPBWHQ5.solutions.bluegull.aqi); kSecAttrAccessGroup added to SystemKeychain.baseAttributes via the new KeychainAccessGroup.shared constant; 10h.13's 'no access group' review conclusion revised in place rather than quietly dropped; ComplianceTests.testKeychainItemHasNoSharedAccessGroup inverted into testKeychainAccessGroupIsOnlyTheOneExpectedSharedGroup (permits exactly the one known group, catches a second/broader/typo'd one); new ComplianceTests.testNoRequestURLLogging guards CLAUDE.md's stated likeliest-leak vector, which now exists in two processes. Build succeeds with automatic provisioning; 169 tests pass.

STILL TO VERIFY BY HAND (Steve): enter an AirNow key in Settings, switch to Direct mode, confirm a widget pinned to an uncached location fetches successfully. Also note the pre-existing item (if any) was stored WITHOUT an access group, so it won't be found after this change and the key must be re-entered once -- the security CLI can't confirm whether one exists, since the item is iCloud-synchronizable (see doc/DEVINSTALL.md).
close_reason: Verified end-to-end by Steve 2026-08-05: Direct mode fetches successfully from both the menu bar app and a widget, using the shared Keychain access group added earlier today. Confirmed the fetch is genuinely direct-to-AirNow (not silently falling back to Service) by disabling the backend Lambda during the test and still getting results. Acceptance criteria met.

title: Revisit service-enable once real Lambda reserved concurrency is restored (q9r.36)
description: service-enable currently calls 'aws lambda delete-function-concurrency', which removes any reservation entirely -- correct right now, since the deployed state has none (bluegull-aqi-q9r.35's workaround). But once q9r.36 lands and template.yaml/samconfig.toml go back to a real positive LambdaReservedConcurrentExecutions value, delete-function-concurrency would undo that real reservation instead of restoring it -- CloudFormation would think the function has its declared reservation, but delete-function-concurrency would have removed it out-of-band. service-enable needs to re-apply the template's actual declared value (e.g. via put-function-concurrency with that value, or simply re-running sam deploy, which is idempotent) once real reservations are back, not just clear the override.

title: Add make targets for service deploy/delete/enable/disable
description: Steve asked for the four operational commands discussed (deploy, delete/undeploy, enable, disable-as-kill-switch) to be real make targets rather than commands to remember/copy-paste.
close_reason: Added deploy/delete/enable/disable targets to service/Makefile (real implementations, ENV-parameterized, defaults to dev) and thin service-deploy/service-delete/service-enable/service-disable wrappers to the root Makefile (matching the existing test-service delegation pattern). enable/disable operate outside CloudFormation via aws lambda put-function-concurrency/delete-function-concurrency, looking up the deployed Lambda's physical name dynamically via aws cloudformation describe-stack-resource -- no hardcoded function name, works across dev/stage/prod via ENV=. title: Large widget AQI number doesn't scale with Dynamic Type; accessibility snapshot test can never fail
description:
Discovered while showing widget screenshots: large-typical-accessibility-dynamic-type.png is byte-for-byte identical (same MD5) to large-typical.png. The snapshot test (BluegullAQIWidgetSnapshotTests.swift:122-123) applies .environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, .accessibility3) before rendering, but the resulting image is 100% unchanged from the non-accessibility variant -- not just the fixed-size number, the ENTIRE render, suggesting the environment override isn't propagating through the ImageRenderer harness at all, not only affecting the one hardcoded font.

Two distinct problems:
1. Accessibility gap: the headline AQI number in LargeWidgetLayout uses a fixed-size font (BluegullAQIWidgetView.swift:175, .font(.system(size: 32, weight: .semibold, design: .rounded))) instead of a Dynamic-Type-aware semantic style, unlike .subheadline/.caption used elsewhere in the same view. Users with larger text accessibility settings get no benefit for the most prominent element in the widget.
2. Test coverage gap: the accessibility snapshot test can never fail regardless of what changes, since its golden image is identical to a different test's golden image -- it provides zero actual regression coverage today.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Root-cause why .environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, ...) doesn't visibly affect the ImageRenderer output at all (harness issue vs. WidgetKit/ImageRenderer platform limitation). 2. If it's fixable, make the large AQI number scale appropriately with Dynamic Type (or document why WidgetKit widgets deliberately don't support it, if that's a real platform constraint). 3. The accessibility snapshot test's golden image must differ from large-typical.png once fixed, so it's actually exercising something.
close_reason: Root-caused: ImageRenderer does not honor .environment(\.dynamicTypeSize, ...) at all on this platform -- confirmed via an isolated repro independent of this codebase (bare Text().font(.caption) renders byte-identical regardless of the override; colorScheme override on the same pipeline works fine, per testLargeTypicalDarkMode). Fixed the real accessibility gap anyway: small/medium/large widget layouts now use @ScaledMetric instead of a fixed .system(size:) font for the headline AQI number, so it correctly scales on a real widget host even though our headless harness can't verify it. Removed the misleading testLargeTypicalAccessibilityDynamicType snapshot test (could never fail -- its golden image was always identical to large-typical's) and its orphaned PNG, with a doc comment explaining why. Folded real verification into bluegull-aqi-mtm.9's scope. make test-swift passes (125 tests + BluegullAQITests suite); no other golden images changed (ScaledMetric's default matches the old hardcoded sizes exactly).

title: Label displayed values as NowCast, not a spot reading
description:
AirNow's real-time observations are NowCast AQI -- EPA's endorsed method for relating short-term data to the AQI. It uses a VARIABLE averaging window: longer when air quality is stable, shorter when changing fast (PM2.5 ~12h stable / ~3h variable; ozone ~8h stable / ~1h variable).

So the number is a weighted average designed to track lived experience -- NOT an instantaneous sensor reading, and NOT the daily AQI (which requires a full 24 hours and is what agencies report for 'yesterday'). UI copy must not imply otherwise: avoid phrasing like 'right now' or 'current reading' that suggests a spot measurement.

'Current Air Quality' is the phrasing airnow.gov itself uses and is safe. This is a copy/labeling task, plus deciding whether to surface a brief explanation of NowCast somewhere reachable (natural fit alongside the preliminary-data disclaimer in the popover/expand view). See doc/DESIGN.md 'What the number is: NowCast, not a spot reading'.
close_reason: Added NowCastCopy.headline ('Current Air Quality', airnow.gov's own phrasing, verified safe) plus a ComplianceTests guard (matching the 10h.17 pattern) scanning Sources/ for the exact unsafe phrases the issue calls out ('right now', 'current reading', etc.) so UI code can't silently regress to spot-reading-implying wording. Verified the guard actually catches a violation via temporary injection, not just that it passes today. Deliberately left the longer NowCast explanation string undefined -- placement/wording for a detail view is a UI decision for e70.11/mtm.14, which don't exist yet. 27/27 tests pass via swift test.

title: Handle AQI > 500 (beyond the AQI scale) as valid data
description:
The category model currently has no representation for AQI above 500, so the default behavior is a blank/unknown category -- which would black out the app during exactly the conditions that produce such readings. That is the failure mode to design against.

RESOLVED: >500 is rare but REAL DATA, not an error.
  - TAD Table 1 bounds Hazardous at 301-500; above that is 'Beyond the AQI', where a value 'can still be computed to indicate relative magnitude' using the Hazardous breakpoints, and users should 'follow the recommendations for the Hazardous category'. NowCast handles it no differently. EPA would not document a computation for something that could only be a fault.
  - It has actually occurred in official reporting: Oregon DEQ recorded Bend above 500 on 2020-09-12 ('beyond the AQI scale' in their words), Newport 'well over 500', during that September's wildfires.
  - We never compute AQI (bluegull-aqi-10h.17), so anything received has already passed AirNow's own QA. Data trustworthiness is upstream of us; our obligation is to disseminate as received.

EARLIER ERROR CORRECTED: a previous version of this issue claimed airnow.gov diverged from the TAD by showing '301 +'. Wrong -- that came from a collapsed text extraction. The expanded AQI Legend panel shows '301 - 500  Hazardous' plus 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale'. Both sources agree; there is no conflict to resolve.

IMPLEMENT: display the actual value; keep maroon (#7E0023) and the Hazardous health guidance per the TAD's explicit direction; indicate it is beyond the scale, using AirNow's own phrasing ('Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale') rather than inventing wording. Do NOT clamp to 500 -- that would misrepresent the reading and conflicts with 'disseminated as received'.

SEPARATE CONCERN, handle distinctly: genuinely malformed values -- negative AQI, non-numeric, absurd magnitudes -- indicate a parse or transport fault rather than extreme air, and belong in an error state, not the beyond-the-scale path. Don't conflate the two.

Test with a fixture at e.g. AQI 650 to confirm it renders correctly rather than blanking.
close_reason: Fixed a real conflation bug: negative AQI (malformed data) previously fell through the same default case as >500 (real beyond-the-scale data), silently misclassifying corrupted input as extreme air quality. AQICategory.init(aqi:) is now failable, returning nil for negative input; PollutantReading.category updated to flatMap accordingly. Added isBeyondScale and beyondScaleNotice (AirNow's own verbatim phrasing 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale', not invented wording). Deliberately did not add upper-bound implausibility detection -- disseminating AirNow's data as received (10h.17) means not second-guessing magnitude past the one unambiguous boundary (negative). Tested with AQI 650 (matching the real Oregon DEQ 2020 wildfire historical example cited in this issue) confirming it renders as valid data, not blank. 22/22 tests pass via swift test.

title: Derive two-tier attribution text from AirNow response data
description:
AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require credit to go FIRST to the specific state/local/tribal agency, THEN to AirNow/EPA. App precedent is evidence, not the standard itself (see doc/DESIGN.md 'On using EPA's own apps as evidence'): checked live against airnow.gov (2026-07-28, San Francisco), which shows a persistent small footer reading 'Data courtesy of / Bay Area Air District' -- the actual local agency name -- alongside a separate 'EPA and PARTNERS' logo lockup. That's useful evidence the specific agency-name field exists and is populated per location in AirNow's own data, not proof this particular wording/placement is what the guidelines require -- Steve's read of the actual text governs the final call.

Implementation: find the field in currentobservation/latLong (or a companion lookup, e.g. ReportingArea -> agency name) that supplies the agency name shown in this pattern. Produce a 'Data courtesy of {agency}' string per reading in BluegullAQIKit, paired with static EPA/AirNow branding as the second tier. If a location genuinely has no agency name in the response, that's the fallback case -- a generic class credit -- not the default design.

This is the exact match for the two-tier attribution requirement -- 'Data courtesy of {reportingAgency}' can be built directly from this field per reading. No fallback to a generic class credit needed for the common case; only worth handling defensively in case reportingAgency is ever null/missing for some location.

Made reportingAgency optional (String?) since AirNow's contract doesn't guarantee it for every location even though live-tested responses have always included it; attributionText returns nil when missing/blank, falling back to just the static second-tier EPA/AirNow branding (app-level UI content, not this package's job) rather than inventing a placeholder agency name. 25/25 tests pass via swift test.

Access-group conclusion: none should exist -- only the container app needs the raw AirNow key, the widget extension only reads pre-fetched AQI data from AppGroupCache (10h.7), never the key. No group = narrowest scope (this app alone). Documented reasoning in SystemKeychain's doc comment, added a ComplianceTests guard against a shared access group being added later without deliberately revisiting this. 62/62 tests pass.

title: Bound App Group cache retention and review file protection
description: The App Group container holds the user's location history on disk -- the locations matter considerably more than the AQI values do. Bound retention rather than accumulating indefinitely, and review the file protection class on the container.
close_reason: Found a real gap: original AppGroupCache.get() treated an expired entry as a miss but never deleted it, so stale entries accumulated forever, and since cleanup only fired reactively on a get() for that exact key, a never-revisited location would never get cleaned up. Fixed with two mechanisms: (1) expired entries deleted both reactively on get() and proactively across every entry on each put(). (2) hard cap on entry count (maxRetainedEntries=10), evicting oldest-by-fetchedAt when exceeded -- TTL alone only bounds age not count. Added SharedCacheStore.allKeys() so AppGroupCache can enumerate/sweep its own prefixed entries without touching a shared store's other data. File protection: verified against Apple's own Security Guide that macOS has no per-file Data Protection classes like iOS -- Class A is backed by the FileVault volume key on macOS, Class D is unsupported. No per-file protection-class API applies here; documented this conclusion in the doc comment rather than leaving it silently unaddressed. Verified against both the in-memory fake and real UserDefaults. 68/68 tests pass.

title: Rate-limit cache misses separately from overall requests
description: Stronger version of the cache-cardinality defense. Misses are what actually cost money and AirNow quota, so limiting them specifically is more targeted than an overall request cap. Build on top of the coordinate validation and grid-snapping, which are the cheaper first line.
close_reason: Implemented MissRateLimiter: global cache-miss budget gating the AirNow-call chokepoint, atomic under concurrency, wired into aqi_lookup/lambda_handler, tuned via new SAM Parameters. 68/68 tests pass, live-verified over real HTTP against DynamoDB Local.

title: Re-tighten absolute perf ceilings against first real measurements
description: The absolute ceilings in doc/DESIGN.md are component-level estimates (~5-10ms API Gateway HTTP API overhead, ~1-3ms warm invoke, ~8-15ms DynamoDB GetItem with reused connection), not measurements -- nothing was deployed when they were written. Once the dev stage has real numbers, tighten the ceilings to match: a ceiling carrying 2.5x slack isn't doing much work. Expected healthy warm-cached p95 is ~20-30ms, so a 50ms ceiling likely wants to come down to ~35ms. Update both DESIGN.md and perf-baseline.json.

title: Add jittered refresh scheduling to client
description: Hourly refresh means every install would otherwise wake at the top of the hour and synchronize into a server-side spike. Each install derives a stable offset within the hour from a per-install value -- stable rather than re-randomized each refresh, so the interval stays consistent -- spreading load uniformly. Directly reduces peak load on the backend.
close_reason: RefreshScheduler derives a stable per-install offset within the refresh interval (persisted via SharedCacheStore, so container app and widget see the same schedule) and computes the next refresh time on that install's interval-spaced schedule -- spreading load across installs instead of everyone waking at the top of the hour. Offset generated once and persisted, not regenerated per call. Found and fixed a real floating-point precision bug via testing: Date stores time relative to 2001 not 1970, so converting large 'seconds since 1970' values loses low-order precision, making a raw-Double 'strictly after now' check fail intermittently near computed boundaries. Root-caused with an isolated repro script, fixed by doing the strictly-after check and any bump entirely in Date's own domain rather than mixing pre/post-conversion Double representations. Verified with 30 consecutive runs of the specific test, then 3 full-suite runs. 75/75 tests pass via swift test.

title: Gate module import time and package size locally (AWS-free cold-start proxy)
description: Import time and deployment package size are measurable with no deployment and correlate well with Init Duration. Gating them in the ordinary functional CI catches the most common cold-start regression -- someone adding a heavy dependency -- long before the nightly perf run does.
close_reason: New bin/coldstart_gate.py measures import time (fresh subprocess) and .aws-sam/build/AqiFunction package size, wired into service-ci.yml after the build step. Ceilings are generous placeholders (350ms/50MB) documented as needing re-tightening once real measurements exist (q9r.26). Dev-workflow gotcha found 2026-08-01: after a Mac restart, the widget was missing entirely from the widget gallery (not just blank/placeholder). Root cause: the app was built/run from a git worktree checkout, and Xcode's DerivedData path is derived from the project's file path -- building from a different worktree/checkout than a prior run produces a new app bundle path. `lsregister`/`pluginkit` ended up with two conflicting registrations for `solutions.bluegull.aqi.widget` (old path's signature + new path's signature) under the same identifier, which silently broke the widget-extension-point lookup that the widget gallery itself queries (`pluginkit -m -p com.apple.widgetkit-extension` stopped returning it, even though `pluginkit -m -i solutions.bluegull.aqi.widget` still found it fine). A plain restart does not fix this. Fix: stop the app (`make app-stop`), force a full LaunchServices re-scan (`/System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Frameworks/LaunchServices.framework/Support/lsregister -f -R -apps system,local,user`), then rebuild and relaunch (`make app-run`). Expect this to recur any time the app is built from a different worktree/checkout path than the previous run -- not a bug in the app itself.

title: Add AWS WAFv2 rate-based rule for per-IP throttling
description: HTTP API (v2) doesn't support REST API v1 usage-plan/API-key throttling, so use a WAFv2 rate-based rule attached to the API Gateway instead. Known tradeoff: coarser than per-install keys (shared IPs behind CGNAT), chosen deliberately.
notes: Investigated 2026-07-30: AWS's CloudFormation docs for AWS::WAFv2::WebACLAssociation explicitly list supported ResourceArn types as ALB, API Gateway REST API, AppSync, Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, Amplify -- HTTP API (API Gateway v2, what this project's AqiHttpApi actually is) is NOT in that list and not supported. See sourced AWS docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-resource-wafv2-webaclassociation.html
close_reason: Resolved as not viable, not implemented: WAFv2 WebACLAssociation doesn't support HTTP API (v2) per AWS's own current CloudFormation docs -- only REST APIs, ALB, Cognito, AppSync, App Runner, Verified Access, Amplify. title: macOS cache_delete terminates the menu bar app; nothing relaunches it
description:
macOS terminates the menu bar app to purge its container caches, and nothing brings it back.

## Observed

Steve reported the menu bar item vanishing twice (2026-08-29 morning, and again
overnight into 2026-08-30). No crash report, no error, no app-side log activity --
the app just stops existing.

Root cause, confirmed from the unified log both times:

    runningboardd: [app<application.solutions.bluegull.aqi...>:PID] Terminating with context:
    <RBSTerminateContext| code:0xBADDD15C
     explanation:CacheDeleteAppContainerCaches requesting termination assertion for solutions.bluegull.aqi
     reportType:None maxTerminationResistance:NonInteractive ...>

    launchd: exited with exit reason (namespace: 15 code: 0xbaddd15c) - OS_REASON_RUNNINGBOARD

com.apple.cache_delete acquires a system-targeted termination assertion (plus an
RBSPreventLaunchLimitation on the bundle id) before purging an app's
~/Library/Containers/<id>/Data/Library/Caches. RunningBoard then terminates the
app non-interactively. This is routine macOS housekeeping, not a crash -- which
is exactly why there is no crash report and no error.

## Not our bug, but our problem

Full retained history of this happening to us (log show --last 30d):

    2026-08-23 08:51:33
    2026-08-25 17:52:28
    2026-08-27 11:43:08
    2026-08-27 11:55:45
    2026-08-27 23:23:02
    2026-08-29 11:23:07
    2026-08-29 17:23:32

Seven times in eight days. The 2026-08-23 occurrence PREDATES both v0.2.0
(2026-08-25) and v0.2.1 (2026-08-29), so this is not a regression from either
release -- ruled out empirically, and separately by inspection: the only
NSApp.terminate added in 0.2.0..0.2.1 is in CompletelyRemoveButton.performRemoval(),
unreachable without the data wipe that provably did not happen (container prefs
were fully intact after each exit).

We are not being singled out. Same window, same mechanism, other victims:
com.apple.weather.WeatherAppIntents (7x), com.apple.wallpaper.agent (7x),
com.apple.tips.Widget (7x), com.apple.podcasts (7x), com.apple.helpviewer (7x),
net.whatsapp.WhatsApp.ServiceExtension (6x), com.apple.news (3x), us (2x).

Trigger on Steve's machine is chronic disk pressure: 17.8 GB free of 494 GB (96%
full), with cache_delete running at urgency 3 (HIGH) on a ~30-minute cycle.

## Why it hurts us more than it hurts Weather.app

Everything else on that list is transient or on-demand -- a widget, an extension,
an app you reopen when you want it. We are a persistent menu bar agent. When
macOS kills us mid-session we stay dead until the user notices the icon is gone
and manually relaunches. The user experience is "the app silently disappeared,"
with nothing anywhere to explain it.

Extra insult: our container Caches directory is 0 bytes. macOS terminates us to
reclaim nothing at all.

## What to consider (not decided)

- The Launch at Login toggle shipped in v0.2.1 (bluegull-aqi-fvt) is the closest
  thing we have to a mitigation, and it does not cover this: SMAppService.mainApp
  relaunches at LOGIN, not after a mid-session termination.
- A separate SMAppService.agent helper -- already an open question in
  bluegull-aqi-hib.1 for the location-helper decision -- would also be the natural
  place to notice the main app is gone and relaunch it. Worth folding into that
  go/no-go rather than deciding separately.
- A launchd KeepAlive LaunchAgent would do it too, but note the
  RBSPreventLaunchLimitation in the assertion: macOS actively blocks relaunch of
  the bundle id for the duration of the purge, so any watchdog needs a backoff
  rather than a tight respawn loop.
- Doing nothing is a legitimate option. It needs sustained 96%-full disk pressure
  to fire at all; most users will never see it.

Filed from investigation on 2026-08-30. No code change made.

title: Show AirNow maintenance-window notice + friendlier error copy
description:
During AirNow's known recurring maintenance window (last Thursday of each month, 7pm-midnight ET -- see bd memory key 'airnow-monthly-maintenance-window' and related bead bluegull-aqi-ydc), two UX improvements were requested (Steve, 2026-08-25), NOT yet implemented -- deliberately deferred for later:

1. Put up a notice on the detail panel (WidgetDetailView.swift) during the maintenance window itself -- something proactive telling the user 'AirNow is doing scheduled maintenance right now' rather than only reacting after a fetch fails. Needs a way to compute 'are we currently inside the window' (last Thursday of the current month, 7pm-midnight America/New_York) -- watch DST edge cases and that 'last Thursday' isn't the same as 'last week.'

2. Replace the generic AirNowError.requestFailed message ('Couldn't reach AirNow. Check your internet connection.', AirNowError.swift) with something like 'AirNow is in a maintenance window.' specifically WHEN a fetch fails AND we're currently inside the known window -- outside the window, keep the existing generic message (a real network/connectivity failure at other times still warrants the current wording). This is a fetch-failure-time check, distinct from #1's proactive/always-visible notice.

Both items need the same 'is it currently AirNow's maintenance window' predicate -- worth writing once and sharing between them. Scope: cosmetic/informational only, no change to the underlying freshness/TTL/retry behavior (that's already handled per bluegull-aqi-ydc's own investigation).

title: Detect AirNow 'delayed updates' (stale-but-successful responses)
description:
AirNow's monthly maintenance notice (last Thursday of each month, 7pm-midnight ET) warns that during the window, data feeds 'may be unavailable OR have delayed updates.' The unavailability half is already handled fine by the existing freshness/TTL system (AppGroupCache.swift: 1hr soft TTL, 3hr hard TTL) -- a failed fetch already falls back to stale-then-expired states with the existing UI banners.

The 'delayed updates' half is NOT handled at all: if AirNow returns 200 OK with a successful payload but DateObserved/HourObserved reflects data from hours ago (their pipeline backed up, not erroring), the app has no way to detect this. Freshness (AQIFreshness/.fresh/.stale/.expired) is derived purely from fetchedAt (when THIS app's HTTP round-trip succeeded), never from the AirNow observation's own timestamp. A delayed-but-'successful' response gets recorded via cache.recordSuccessfulFetch() and is shown as .fresh for a full new hour -- no banner, no stale indicator -- even though the underlying observation could be hours old. The only way a user would notice is by manually comparing the 'Observed' vs 'Updated' timestamp captions already shown in the popover/widget detail view (AQIPopoverView.swift, WidgetDetailView.swift).

Proposed fix: compare the parsed observedAt (PollutantReading+Observation.swift) against fetchedAt/now at the point a successful fetch is recorded, and demote freshness (or otherwise surface the existing stale-warning banner) when the gap between them is implausibly large for a normal reporting cadence. Needs a product decision on the actual threshold (how old is 'too old' for an observation that arrived via an otherwise-successful fetch) -- this is a real design call, not just an implementation detail, since AirNow's normal reporting cadence/latency baseline should inform it rather than picking an arbitrary number.

Not urgent: this is a once-a-month, ~5-hour window; the cosmetic mismatch (showing an hours-old reading as fresh) is low-stakes for a background widget, consistent with doc/DESIGN.md's own stated philosophy that availability/staleness handling is deliberately not over-engineered for this app.

title: Transient cfprefsd App Group attach failure on dev-build launch
description:
Observed 2026-08-24 while iterating on e70.48's UI layout: a fresh dev-build
launch of BluegullAQI intermittently shows "Pinned Location" instead of a
real pin's name in WidgetDetailView, because PinnedLocationsStore.load()
comes back empty.

Root cause (confirmed via unified log, not guessed): on process start, the
very first UserDefaults(suiteName: "group.solutions.bluegull.aqi") access
hits:

    Couldn't read values in CFPrefsPlistSource... Using kCFPreferencesAnyUser
    with a container is only allowed for System Containers, detaching from
    cfprefsd

...and silently falls back to a DIFFERENT, non-container preferences file
(~/Library/Preferences/group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.plist) instead of the
real, properly-entitled Group Container
(~/Library/Group Containers/group.solutions.bluegull.aqi/...). The fallback
file has real cache/fetch-timestamp data (auto-repopulated by the app's own
fetch loop) but never has pinned-locations (only written on an explicit user
edit), so a pinned widget's detail view finds no match and shows the generic
fallback label.

Confirmed via `stat`/`plutil` that the REAL container's data was NOT lost --
still intact, including the real pinned-locations list, dataSourceMode, etc.
This is purely a resolution/attach problem at a point in time, not data loss.

Confirmed this specific error started only with the FIRST relaunch after
running `make test-swift` interleaved with `make app-run` in the same
session (error first appeared 17:46:31, right after several `make test-swift`
runs which do an UNSIGNED `xcodebuild build`/`test` -only-testing:BluegullAQITests
against the SAME DerivedData the signed `make app-run` build also uses) --
plausible but not proven that the unsigned test build/run confuses
containermanagerd's registration for the bundle ID, causing a subsequent
signed launch to race/fail on its first container-suite attach.

Also confirmed (2026-08-24, same session) that the failure recurs even on a
FULLY clean process restart (both BluegullAQI and the stale BluegullAQIWidget
extension host killed first) -- so it's not just about a lingering stale
widget-host connection either.

Then self-resolved a few minutes later on the SAME running process without
any further action -- Steve confirmed "it's working now" shortly after the
same PID's own launch-time log line showed the failure. So: transient/racy
at launch, not permanently broken for a given process's lifetime.

Not investigated further per Steve's own priority call mid-investigation --
worth revisiting if it recurs and blocks real work, especially the
interleaved test-swift/app-run theory above, which wasn't proven, just
correlated.

title: Single-instance guard silently drops the URL when a widget tap triggers a second launch
description:
Confirmed live 2026-08-24 while testing bluegull-aqi-e70.49: tapping a placed widget's face silently failed to open the "Air Quality Detail" window. Root-caused via a live unified-log capture of the actual tap (`/usr/bin/log stream --predicate 'process == "BluegullAQI" OR process == "launchd" OR process == "BluegullAQIWidget"'`), not guessed.

## Confirmed mechanism

`BluegullAQIApp.init()` (mac-app/BluegullAQI/BluegullAQIApp.swift:70-93) holds a single-instance guard added by bluegull-aqi-e70.25 to stop a second launch from producing a duplicate menu-bar icon:

    let fd = open(lockURL.path, O_CREAT | O_RDWR, 0o600)
    if fd == -1 || flock(fd, LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB) != 0 {
        let bundleID = Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier!
        NSRunningApplication.runningApplications(withBundleIdentifier: bundleID).first?.activate()
        exit(0)
    }

This runs before `body: some Scene` is ever evaluated (the comment directly above it says so explicitly) -- i.e. before the `Window("Air Quality Detail", id: "widget-detail")` scene and its `.onOpenURL` (BluegullAQIApp.swift:144-149) exist at all in this process.

Live capture of a real widget tap showed a fresh process launch (`launchedByLS=1` in the ProcessManager log lines -- confirms it really was LaunchServices dispatching the tap's `bluegullaqi://` URL, not something unrelated), which:
1. Ran the default `@State` initializers (CoreLocation/App Group setup -- visible in the log as a real, if wasted, location-permission-status round trip)
2. Reached the `init()` guard above, found the lock already held by the existing running instance
3. Called `.activate()` on it (visible as `BringForward`/`BringFrontModifier` in the log, `uiElement=1` matching this app's `LSUIElement` status)
4. Called `exit(0)` roughly 100ms after spawning (visible as the CoreAnalytics "Entering/Exiting exit handler" sequence)

`.activate()` only brings the existing process to the front -- it does not forward whatever Apple Event/URL triggered this second launch. So the `bluegullaqi://` URL carrying "open Air Quality Detail for this location" is read by nobody and silently discarded, every time a tap causes a genuinely new process to spawn rather than macOS delivering the Apple Event straight to the already-running instance.

## Two separate layers -- both real, only one is this bead

1. **Why a second process launches at all** (normally macOS should just message the existing running instance instead of spawning a new one): traced this specific session's occurrence to LaunchServices having multiple real, valid `BluegullAQI.app`/`BluegullAQIWidget.appex` registrations simultaneously (old notarized `/Applications` copy, the DerivedData dev build, several stale DMG-mount and `/Users/sbarber/Builds/` entries accumulated from past `make app-package` runs). Manually pruning every registration down to just the current dev build (`lsregister -u` on each stray path) plus a `chronod`/`NotificationCenter` restart made the symptom go away in this session -- confirmed by Steve re-tapping afterward. That's environmental cleanup, not a code fix, and nothing currently prevents the registration mess from recurring (e.g. after the next `make app-package` run, or once distribution is more than one-Mac-at-a-time).
2. **What THIS bead is about**: regardless of why a second launch happens, the code has no path to recover the URL that caused it before exiting. That's a real, independent robustness gap -- worth hardening so a future recurrence (different cause, same shape) doesn't silently eat a user's tap again.

## Suggested fix direction

Before `exit(0)`, check whether this launch was triggered by an Open URL Apple Event (e.g. via `NSAppleEventManager.shared().currentAppleEvent` / the `kAEGetURL` event class, inspectable this early since it doesn't require the run loop to be spinning) and, if so, relay it to the already-activated instance rather than just dropping it -- e.g. `NSWorkspace.shared.open(url, configuration:)` targeted explicitly at the running instance's own `NSRunningApplication`/bundle URL (not a bare re-resolve of the bundle ID, since that's what got confused in the first place), or writing the pending URL through the shared App Group cache for the surviving instance to notice (bluegull-aqi-e70.49's new `CacheChangeBroadcast` mechanism is a plausible, already-built-and-tested vehicle for exactly this kind of "hey, something happened, go check" cross-process signal, though this would be a second, distinct use of it, not literally reused as-is).

Needs a real design pass before implementing, not a quick patch -- confirm the actual Apple Event inspection API works this early in process life (before `NSApplication.shared` is fully spun up) before committing to that approach.
acceptance_criteria: When a second BluegullAQI launch is triggered by an Open URL Apple Event (e.g. a widget tap's bluegullaqi:// deep link) and the single-instance guard in BluegullAQIApp.init() detects an existing running instance, that URL is relayed to the surviving instance (which opens the Air Quality Detail window for it, same as if it had received the URL directly) instead of being silently dropped. A plain second launch with no URL still just activates the existing instance and exits, unchanged. Design for the actual relay mechanism confirmed before implementing (see the two candidate approaches noted in the description) -- this needs verifying the chosen API actually works this early in process life, not an assumption.

title: Remove redundant Done button from Settings panel
description:
Steve (2026-08-19): the Settings window's 'Done' button (mac-app/BluegullAQI/SettingsView.swift:71, Button("Done") { dismissWindow(id: "settings") }) is redundant with the window's own title-bar close button. Confirmed not an Apple HIG convention -- standard macOS Settings/Preferences windows (System Settings, Mail, Safari, Xcode, SwiftUI's built-in Settings {} scene) rely solely on the window chrome (close button / Cmd+W), never an in-content Done button; that pattern is iOS-sheet-specific, where there's no window chrome to dismiss. No design rationale found in doc/DESIGN.md or git history for why this one was added -- looks incidental, not deliberate.

Remove the button (and its surrounding Divider() if now orphaned). Also update BluegullAQIUITests/BluegullAQIUITests.swift:51, which currently does app.buttons["settingsDoneButton"].click() to close the window -- switch it to closing via the window's standard close control (or Cmd+W) instead.

title: Settings panel is too wide
description:
Steve's feedback (pre-release 0.1.0 direct build, 2026-08-19): the Settings window (mac-app/BluegullAQI/SettingsView.swift:111, currently .frame(minWidth: 420, idealWidth: 460)) is excessively wide.

Note the doc comment directly above that line: a prior fixed .frame(width: 360) was deliberately replaced with this wider min/ideal range because 360pt truncated DataSourceModeToggle's segmented-control labels, and .windowResizability(.contentSize) derives the window's resizable range from the content's own reported size range (a single fixed width made the window non-resizable). Narrowing back down needs to either shrink/rewrap the segmented control's labels first or otherwise reduce the content's own natural width -- just lowering the frame numbers without addressing that will reintroduce the truncation this same code was written to fix.

title: App Store review implications of the helper agent
description:
Bundling and registering a LaunchAgent via SMAppService is permitted for App Store apps (macOS 13+), but it changes the submission in ways worth getting right before bluegull-aqi-fw4.4:

- Helper must be sandboxed with its own entitlements, and the App Group/keychain groups must match the app's.
- Privacy nutrition label (bluegull-aqi-fw4.2) needs to reflect that a background process collects location.
- Review notes should explain WHY a background agent is necessary -- namely that widget extensions cannot resolve location on macOS and Apple's own Weather widget only manages it via the private com.apple.locationd.effective_bundle. A reviewer may reasonably ask why the app can't just do it.
- Blocked on the go/no-go decision; irrelevant if option 1 or 2 wins.
acceptance_criteria: Helper passes validation as part of the archive, entitlements are consistent across app and helper, and the privacy label covers background location collection.

title: Remove dead widget-requested-* keys left in the App Group by the deleted o4b relay
description:
Observed live in the real App Group container while debugging on 2026-08-11 (~/Library/Group Containers/group.solutions.bluegull.aqi/Library/Preferences/group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.plist):

  widget-requested-locations
  widget-requested-current-location-last-seen

These are remnants of the WidgetRequestedLocationsStore / widgetSettleLoop / activeWidgetLocations relay that bluegull-aqi-mtm.24 deleted once widgets could self-fetch pinned locations. The authoritative path is ~/Library/Group Containers/group.solutions.bluegull.aqi/Library/Preferences/group.solutions.bluegull.aqi.plist, readable with plutil -p.

title: Give BluegullAQIWidget.appex its own compiled AppIcon (Activity Monitor shows blank)
description: Follow-up to bluegull-aqi-b3r/6qy (real app icon + widget gallery icon-cache fix). The widget extension process (BluegullAQIWidget.appex, runs as its own process visible in Activity Monitor) shows a blank/generic icon there -- confirmed the .appex bundle has zero icon resources of its own (no Assets.car, no AppIcon.icns, no icon keys in its Info.plist), unlike the container app which now has a correctly compiled AppIcon. Activity Monitor resolves a process's icon from its own bundle, not the container app's, for extension processes. Fix: point the BluegullAQIWidget xcodegen target at the same mac-app/BluegullAQI/Assets.xcassets directory as an additional sources entry (no file duplication -- one shared source compiled into both targets' own Assets.car) and set ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME there too.
acceptance_criteria: After a real signed build, BluegullAQIWidget.appex/Contents/Resources contains Assets.car (or AppIcon.icns) with the real icon, and the BluegullAQIWidget process shows the BlueGull gull icon in Activity Monitor instead of a blank/generic one.
notes:
Follow-up finding (2026-08-11, after a full make app-package -> notarize -> reinstall -> widget-reset round-trip): Activity Monitor STILL shows no icon for BluegullAQIWidget, even though the running /Applications build's .appex was directly confirmed (again) to have the correct Assets.car/AppIcon.icns and CFBundleIconName/CFBundleIconFile Info.plist keys, correctly Developer-ID signed. Ruled out caching: restarting Activity Monitor itself, and separately restarting iconservicesagent (the per-user IconServices cache daemon), changed nothing.

Root cause is NOT a packaging defect -- per a GitHub issue about another app's WidgetsExtension.appex (exelban/stats#2901) and general research, Activity Monitor does not resolve custom icons for app-extension (.appex) processes at all; it appears to be inherent OS behavior for this class of process, not something an app's own bundle can override. The icon work here is still correct/worth keeping (matches best practice, matters for any other context that does look it up), but there is no further fix available for the original Activity Monitor symptom -- closing this line of investigation.

title: widget-reset doesn't clear the widget gallery's stale icon (NotificationCenter caches it separately)
description: Confirmed live (2026-08-11): after adding a real AppIcon (bluegull-aqi-b3r) and installing a fresh notarized build to /Applications, the 'Add Widgets' gallery picker still showed a blank placeholder icon next to BluegullAQI in the source list, even after 'make widget-reset' + killing/relaunching the app. Root cause: the gallery UI is drawn by /System/Library/CoreServices/NotificationCenter.app, a long-running process that caches the icon it first resolved for the app (from before AppIcon.appiconset existed) -- separate from chronod (the widget host, already handled by widget-reset) and separate from LaunchServices' own registration (also already handled). Confirmed the app bundle itself had the correct icon compiled in the whole time (Assets.car/AppIcon.icns present, codesigned Developer ID build) -- this was purely a stale-cache-in-a-long-lived-process issue. 'killall NotificationCenter' (it auto-relaunches, safe) fixed it immediately.
acceptance_criteria: make widget-reset also kills NotificationCenter (or the fix is otherwise folded in), with a comment explaining why, matching the existing chronod-restart reasoning already in that target.
close_reason: Added 'killall NotificationCenter' to widget-reset -- confirmed via Steve testing live: the widget gallery picker (drawn by NotificationCenter.app, a long-running system agent) caches the icon it first resolved for the app, independent of chronod/LaunchServices which widget-reset already handled. Verified by actually running 'make widget-reset' after the fix and confirming it executes cleanly.

title: Verify current WAF rate-based rule minimums
description: The design references per-IP rate limiting without pinning down the current minimum threshold and evaluation window AWS supports for rate-based rules; these have changed over time. Confirm the actual numbers before relying on them, since they determine how much protection the rule really provides.
close_reason: Moot: depended on q9r.5, which was resolved as not viable (WAF can't attach to an HTTP API v2). Its underlying question was answered incidentally anyway while researching q9r.5: RateBasedStatement.Limit min=10/max=2e9, EvaluationWindowSec allows 60/120/300/600 (default 300) -- recorded in doc/DESIGN.md changelog for reference if CloudFront+WAF (q9r.33) happens later.

title: Evaluate CloudFront in front of the API
description:
Deliberately deferred, not rejected. The response is identical for everyone in a region and changes hourly -- close to an ideal CDN workload. CloudFront would absorb most traffic at the edge before it reaches Lambda, cutting cost and attack surface together, and offers better DDoS absorption than raw API Gateway. Not worth the complexity pre-launch; this is the natural first move if scale materializes. Revisit when sustained traffic justifies it or if cost-attack exposure becomes a live concern.

REGION GOTCHA if this is ever picked up: the API itself deploys to us-east-2, but CloudFront's ACM certificate MUST be requested in us-east-1 specifically -- a hard, non-negotiable CloudFront-wide rule, completely independent of which region the origin (API Gateway) runs in. This means adopting CloudFront would require a SECOND cert in us-east-1 alongside the existing us-east-2 cert used directly by the HttpApi custom domain, not a replacement for it.

description:
Auto-update / ask-first / manual-check mechanism for the direct (non-App-Store) build, most likely via Sparkle (https://sparkle-project.org/), the de facto standard for this on macOS. Sparkle's default UX is ask-first, matching the preferred behavior.
